docs.title: compliance
docs.text:
Feature: Compliance

The accepted scenarios of this context: gap analysis of documents against the checklists of the applicable standards, and the checklists RDM ships. Each is stamped with an item id that is never renumbered or reused, and verified by the acceptance tests whose Allure results carry that id as a tag label.

Rule: A document set has a gap for every checklist key no document references

item-05-001 ✓ verified · 1 run Gap analysis names each missing reference and exits non-zero when one is missing or nothing was checked

Given a checklist "cl.txt" with the clauses X-1 and X-2 When the regulatory author runs rdm gap cl.txt over "partial.md", which references [[X-1]] only Then it exits 3, listing X-2 and not X-1, under the heading "# 1 gap:" And over "full.md", which references [[X-1]] and [[X-2]], it exits 0 And a stray "[[" does not turn the next paragraphs' mentions into references: X-2 is still missing And a bare mention "We do not address X-2" is no reference to X-2: it exits 3 And [[X-12]] does not reference the key X-1: it exits 3 And [[FDA-SW:sdmp: This document is a pointer document.]] references the key FDA-SW:sdmp: it exits 0 And [[FDA-SW:sdmp]] does not reference the key FDA-SW: it exits 3 And a byte-order mark is not part of the first key: a checklist beginning with a byte-order mark before "X-1 first" is covered by full.md And "include cl.txt " with spaces around the name is resolved When nothing could be checked: a checklist with no clauses, a checklist that does not exist, a bare "include", an include of a file that does not exist, a document that does not exist, or a directory given as a document Then it exits 2, never 0 When a document covering every clause still holds a "TODO: write this section" placeholder Then it exits 0 and warns, naming the document and its placeholder When its report of 20000 gaps is piped into a reader that stops after one line Then it ends quietly, with no traceback and no BrokenPipe error

Covers: rule Gap (success) · rule Gap (refusal 1) · rule Gap (refusal 2) · rule Gap (refusal 3) · need compliance/gap-analysis

Rule: RDM ships composable checklists for the applicable standards

item-05-002 ✓ verified · 1 run The built-in checklists are listed by name, hold unique keys and resolve their includes

When the regulatory author lists the built-in checklists Then 62304_2015_class_b, 14971_2019, FDA-SW_2021_enhanced and csv_tool_validation (computer software validation of a tool) are listed by name And IEC 62304, ISO 14971, FDA-SW, FDA-CYBER and FDA-HFE each have a built-in checklist with clauses And no built-in checklist holds a key twice And 62304_2015_class_b, which includes 62304_2015_class_a by name, requires every clause of class A and more Given a checklist "main.txt" with "include base.txt" and the clause M-1, and "base.txt" with the clause B-1 When a document referencing only [[M-1]] is checked against main.txt Then it exits 3: B-1, defined only in the included file, is still required And a document referencing [[M-1]] and [[B-1]] exits 0 Given "a.txt" includes "sub/b.txt", which includes "../a.txt" and "./../a.txt" When the coverage of a document referencing [[A-1]] is reported against a.txt Then a.txt is read once: its row is "| A.TXT | 2 | 1 | 1 | 50% |" and it exits 3

Covers: guarantee BuiltInChecklistsCompose · need compliance/gap-analysis

Rule: Coverage of a document set is tabulated per checklist

item-05-003 ✓ verified · 1 run The coverage report gives each checklist's total, missing, covered and percent

Given a checklist "iso_checklist.txt" with the clauses ISO-1, ISO-2 and ISO-3 When the regulatory author reports coverage of "process.md", which references [[ISO-1]] and [[ISO-3]] Then the row "| ISO | 3 | 1 | 2 | 66% |" is printed and it exits 3 And in verbose mode the missing ISO-2 is named When the coverage of a document referencing all three clauses is reported Then it exits 0, and in verbose mode prints no empty "Missing Items" heading When the checklist has no clauses or does not exist Then it exits 2: nothing could be checked

Covers: rule Coverage (success) · rule Coverage (refusal 1) · need compliance/gap-analysis

Rule: RDM keeps its own record under the 21 CFR Part 11 checklist it ships

item-05-004 ✓ verified · 1 run RDM's own document-control statement passes the built-in Part 11 checklist, and fails without a control

When the regulatory author lists the built-in checklists Then part11_document_control is listed by name When dhf/documents/document_control.md is checked against part11_document_control Then it exits 0: the statement references every clause When a copy of the statement without its reference [[P11:11.10e]] is checked Then it exits 3: dropping one control fails the audit

Covers: guarantee Part11ChecklistShipped · need compliance/gap-analysis

docs.title: graph
docs.text:
Feature: Graph

The accepted scenarios of this context: the record projected into an RDF graph that people query and explore and agents read, never edit. Each is stamped with an item id that is never renumbered or reused, and verified by the acceptance tests whose Allure results carry that id as a tag label.

Rule: The record is projected into one named graph per source, deterministically

item-06-001 ✓ verified · 1 run A committed record becomes a dataset of named graphs, byte-identical while the record is unchanged

Given a committed repository whose spec holds the needs Alarm and Logging as Features and the requirements item-01-001 and item-01-002 under them And controlled documents with id, title and revision, and Allure results When the author builds the graph Then the record graph holds each user need with its Feature's title as id and its description as text And each requirement with its text, the needs it addresses, its context and its source line, and each bounded context And read through an adapter (Löyly's layout, Allium), the graph holds what a need faces, provides and guarantees, the rules a requirement covers, the Allium rules, and a context with no requirement And each controlled document with its id, title and revision And an executions graph only when results are given And a git graph with the design document's latest commit, its time and its author And an rdfs:label on every typed node And an ontology graph of RDM's vocabulary, reusing OSLC RM And the dataset is written as sorted N-Quads, byte-identical for an unchanged record And a literal holding a Unicode line separator stays one statement

Covers: guarantee RecordProjectedPerSource · need graph/explore-graph

Rule: The projection is stored, queried and served read-only

item-06-002 ✓ verified · 1 run The store is replaced on each build, queried with SPARQL and served read-only

Given a graph built into a store from a record with item-01-001 and item-01-002 When the author queries the store with the standard prefixes undeclared and no GRAPH clause Then the query answers over the union of the named graphs When item-01-002 is removed and the graph is built again Then the store holds no item-01-002: it was replaced, not merged And with no store given, the query answers from an in-memory projection, ASK and CONSTRUCT included And a SPARQL Update or a SERVICE call is refused: nothing changes, nothing reaches the network And FROM, which the union default graph would ignore, is refused, and so is SERVICE with a variable endpoint, while a prefix named service is no call When the store is served over HTTP Then the endpoint's default graph is the union, the standard prefixes are predeclared and CORS is open And an update from another origin is refused and the data stays And SERVICE is refused, even after a comment ended by a carriage return And the endpoint answers from the last build And a store that does not exist is refused, not created

Covers: guarantee StoreQueriedAndServedReadOnly · need graph/explore-graph

Rule: Checklists join the graph as data

item-06-003 ✓ verified · 1 run A text checklist, a built-in one and an RDF one become SKOS collections of clauses

Given a text checklist that includes a built-in checklist by name, and a checklist written in RDF When the author builds the graph with those checklists Then each checklist is a SKOS collection of its own clauses that links the checklists it includes And the built-in checklist is resolved by its name And each clause has its key, description, standard, edition and nearest listed parent clause And the RDF checklist is loaded as it is, its nodes labelled like any other

Covers: guarantee ChecklistsAsSkos · need graph/explore-graph

item-06-009 ✓ verified · 1 run A document's reference tags link it to the clauses rdm gap would match

Given documents whose [[...]] tags reference some clauses of a checklist and not others When the author builds the graph with that checklist Then each document links to the clauses its tags reference, matched as rdm gap matches keys And the clauses no document references are exactly those rdm gap reports missing

Covers: guarantee DocumentsLinkTheirClauses · need graph/explore-graph

Rule: The gate rules hold over the graph as SHACL shapes

item-06-004 ✓ verified · 1 run The shapes block exactly what the release gate blocks, each finding on its node

Given records with the requirements item-01-001 and item-01-002, each with these needs and runs:

case needs runs blocked all pass Need1, Need2 item-01-001 passed; item-01-002 passed nothing failed Need1, Need2 item-01-001 passed and failed; item-01-002 passed item-01-001 broken Need1, Need2 item-01-001 passed and broken; item-01-002 passed item-01-001 untested Need1, Need2 item-01-001 passed item-01-002 skipped only Need1, Need2 item-01-001 passed; item-01-002 skipped item-01-002 unaddressed need Need1, Need2, Need3 item-01-001 passed; item-01-002 passed Need3

When the shapes are validated over each record's graph and the release gate is run on it Then for each case both block exactly what the table names When the needs are Need1, Need2 and Need3 and item-01-001's only run failed Then Need3 is a violation "user need is addressed by no requirement" And item-01-001 is a violation "requirement has a failed or broken test run" And item-01-002 is a violation "requirement is not verified by any passing test run" And a checklist clause no document references, and a clause without a key or a standard, are violations And a requirement addressing no user need, and a run claiming an id that is no requirement, are warnings And what the release gate blocks about the whole record, the shapes block too And the executions graph reads results as the gates do: a byte-order mark is read, a failed step fails its run

Covers: guarantee GateRulesAsShapes · need graph/explore-graph

item-06-010 ✓ verified · 1 run rdm graph validate reports each result and exits on a violation

Given a record whose graph has violations, and one without When the author runs rdm graph validate on each Then each result is a line with its severity, focus node and message And the command exits 1 on the record with violations and 0 on the other And a user-supplied shapes file adds its rules as data When a shapes or checklist file is not RDF Then the command reports an error and exits 2, never with a traceback

Covers: rule GraphValidate (success) · rule GraphValidate (refusal 1) · rule GraphValidate (refusal 2) · need graph/explore-graph

Rule: The graph can be opened in AWS Graph Explorer as a file

item-06-005 ✓ verified · 1 run The whole record is written as a Graph Explorer file, a class left out on request

Given a record with needs, requirements, documents, risks and test runs When the author writes the graph as a Graph Explorer file Then the file has Graph Explorer's envelope and connection And every node of the record, of every kind, and nothing from the vocabulary And every link between two record nodes, in Graph Explorer's edge-id form, and no rdf:type statement When a class is left out Then its nodes and their links are dropped, with the nodes that hang only from them, and only those And the command writes the file from a fresh projection or from a built store When a class to leave out is one the graph does not have Then it is refused, naming the classes the graph has

Covers: rule ExplorerFile (success) · rule ExplorerFile (refusal 1) · need graph/explore-graph

Rule: An agent reads the record through four read-only tools

item-06-006 ✓ verified · 1 run The agent server answers schema, query, trace and validate from the current record

Given a record with the needs Alarm and Logging, the requirements item-01-001 and item-01-002, and a passing run of item-01-001 When an agent connects to rdm graph mcp Then it is offered exactly four tools: schema, query, trace and validate And schema gives the vocabulary and the predeclared prefixes And query answers SPARQL with those prefixes predeclared And trace of item-01-001 gives its scenario, context, source, needs, coverage and runs And trace of a need gives its text, context and requirements, and what an adapter adds (faces, provides, guarantees) is empty And validate gives the gate shapes' results: item-01-002 has no passing run When the record is edited during the session Then the next call answers from the edited record

Covers: rule ServeAgent (success) · need graph/agent-reads-record

item-06-007 ✓ verified · 1 run The agent server cannot change the record or reach the network

Given the agent server over a record Then its four tools are all declared read-only and non-destructive When the agent sends every form of SPARQL Update Then each is refused and nothing in the record changed When the agent sends SERVICE in any case, with an IRI or a variable endpoint Then it is refused, while the word inside a literal is just text When the agent traces input that is not id-shaped Then it is refused as "not an id" And trace answers an id the record declares whatever its shape, such as the need Logging, and nothing built from it And SELECT, ASK, CONSTRUCT and DESCRIBE all work And rows beyond the cap are cut and the cut is reported; under the cap nothing is flagged

Covers: guarantee AgentCannotChangeTheRecord · need graph/agent-reads-record

Rule: Risks are in the graph, with shapes that block what the release gate blocks

item-06-008 ✓ verified · 1 run Each risk's facts are in the risks graph, and the shapes block the risks the gate blocks

Given a risk register with safety and security risks, their scores, controls and acceptances, and a risk policy When the graph is built Then the risks graph holds each risk's facts: category, STRIDE category, linked risks, hazard, situation, harm, scores, levels, residual decision, status, controls and acceptance And the residual decision is "not evaluated" until every control has a passing test And trace gives a risk with each controlling requirement, and a requirement with the risks it controls And the shapes block exactly the risks the release gate blocks, case by case When the risk policy is malformed Then the gate blocks, and the shapes block every risk with its message When a risk has no id Then the gate blocks it, and so do the shapes, on a stand-in node When a finding about the register has no risk to carry it Then the gate blocks, and so do the shapes, on a stand-in node for the register

Covers: guarantee RisksProjectedWithShapes · need risk/risk-register

item-06-012 ✓ verified · 1 run A risk links to the document of the policy it was evaluated against

Given a risk register and a document declaring the risk policy When the graph is built Then each risk links to the policy's document And without a policy, a risk links to none

Covers: guarantee RiskLinkedToItsPolicy · need graph/explore-graph

Rule: Each controlled document carries who landed its latest change

item-06-011 ✓ verified · 1 run A document's latest change is recorded with the commit that landed it on the default branch

Given a change to SDS-1 on a feature branch, which goes on after the change while main moves on When someone else merges the branch into main, and later work lands on main Then SDS-1's latest change is authored on the branch and landed by the merge, with the merge's author And the landing is still the merge, not the newest commit When a change is on a branch that has not landed Then the document has no landing facts and a warning names it When the latest change is a direct commit on main Then it landed in itself, by its own author, and nothing warns And every controlled document has its commit and landing, the V&V plan as well as the design documents And in a repository with no remote whose one branch is neither main nor master, that branch is the default

Covers: guarantee LandingCommitRecorded · need graph/explore-graph

Rule: A run carries what it recorded, and nothing the record already holds

item-06-013 ✓ verified · 1 run A run's steps and attachments are in the graph and in trace

Given an Allure result with nested steps and attachments on the run and on a step When the graph is built Then the run carries its steps in order and nested, each with its name and status And its attachments, on the run and on the step, each with its name, media type and file And trace lists them with the run, nested and ordered

Covers: guarantee StepsAndAttachmentsCarried · need graph/explore-graph

item-06-014 ✓ verified · 1 run A result is projected in full, but not what claims nothing about design controls

Given a failed Allure result with a uuid, a full name, start and stop times, a status message and trace, parameters, labels and links, and a container with fixtures When the graph is built Then the run carries its uuid, name and times, its status message and trace, and its parameters as name and value And its labels are not nodes, its links, a test case per history id and the container fixtures are not projected And its item tag and output labels still link the run to its requirement and its code

Covers: guarantee OnlyDesignControlFactsProjected · need graph/explore-graph

Rule: Bounded contexts and documents link to each other from the record

item-06-015 ✓ verified · 1 run Contexts link to the documents that declare them, and documents to the ones they reference

Given design documents whose frontmatter declares contexts with their part and references other documents When the graph is built Then each bounded context links to the document whose contexts frontmatter declares it, with its part And each controlled document links to the controlled documents its references frontmatter names And the traceability matrix template, an output, is not projected And once any document declares contexts, a shape warns on a context no document declares And validation fails on a reference to a document the record does not hold And a context may be declared by id alone, and a single reference may be a string

Covers: guarantee ContextsLinkedToTheirDocuments · need graph/explore-graph

Rule: Evidence is tied to the version of the product it tested

item-06-016 ✓ verified · 2 runs Each run links to the commit it tested, and a run of another commit than the product's is stale

Given a record at commit HEAD, and runs labelled with HEAD (one clean, one dirty), with an older commit, and with none When the graph is built and validated Then each run links to the commit its commit label names And the record carries the commit it was built at and the product's commit, its own And the run of uncommitted changes is marked and the clean one is not And a shape warns on the run tied to no commit And a shape warns on the run of the older commit: another commit than the product's When the spec lives in a repository of its own Then the product's commit is that repository's, the record's stays its own And a run of the product's commit is current, and a run of the record's commit is stale

Covers: guarantee EvidenceTiedToTheProductCommit · need graph/explore-graph

docs.title: publishing
docs.text:
Feature: Publishing

The accepted scenarios of this context: compiling the design history file from the record (templates and data to Markdown, its filters, its post-processing, snippets from source), RDM's own user manual, and the generated release documents (the device-master-record index and the verification report). Each is stamped with an item id that is never renumbered or reused, and verified by the acceptance tests whose Allure results carry that id as a tag label.

Rule: A document is a Markdown template rendered against the data files supplied, never against a value they lack

item-07-001 ✓ verified · 1 run rdm render fills a Markdown template from data files, each under its file name

Given a template doc.md "# {{ device.name }}" then "Version {{ device.version }}, by {{ other.maker }}." And the data files empty.yml, device.yml with name "Acme Monitor" and version "1.2", and other.yml with maker "Acme Inc" When the regulatory author runs rdm render doc.md with empty.yml, device.yml and other.yml Then the output is "# Acme Monitor", then "Version 1.2, by Acme Inc." When other.yml is left out Then rendering is refused with exit status 2, naming "other" and doc.md When the template nope.md does not exist Then rendering is refused with exit status 2, naming nope.md

Covers: rule Render (success) · rule Render (refusal 1) · rule Render (refusal 2) · need publishing/compile-dhf

Rule: Templates have the filters a traceability table needs

item-07-002 ✓ verified · 1 run invert_dependencies, join_to, md_indent, glob, include and gherkin build traceability tables and final documents

Given items with id A depending on B When a template inverts them with invert_dependencies('id', 'deps') Then B is depended on by ['A'] Given a table with rows r1 (v 1) and r2 (v 2) When a template joins ['r2', 'r1'] to it with join_to Then it reads the rows in that order: "2;1;" When a template indents the snippet "# Title" with md_indent(header_shift=1) Then it reads "## Title" Given feature files spec/b/spec.feature ("Feature: B") and spec/a/spec.feature, and a document arch.md with frontmatter id SDS-1 and the heading "# Architecture" When a template includes every file 'spec/*/spec.feature' | glob gives, and 'arch.md' | include | md_indent(1) Then it carries spec/a/spec.feature, then spec/b/spec.feature, each as written, and "## Architecture" without the frontmatter Given a feature file with a Rule "Within 2 s", a scenario tagged @smoke @allium-rule-success.Raise @REQ-12 whose steps hold "\$140" and "\<value>", an outline @REQ-13 with Examples, and a comment When a template lays it out with gherkin, given verification data in which REQ-12 is verified by 2 runs Then it is Markdown marked for the templates: the Rule a rule-line, each scenario a scenario-card led by its id and, for REQ-12, "✓ verified · 2 runs", its steps' keywords marked, the outline's Examples a table, what its tags cover in words ("rule Raise (success)", "need Alarm"), "\$" and "\<" escaped, and the comment left out When rdm render joins the id r9 to a table holding only r1 Then rendering exits with status 2, naming r9

Covers: guarantee TraceabilityFilters · need publishing/compile-dhf

Rule: Rendered Markdown is post-processed: numbered, given its own words, and stripped of auditor-only notes

item-07-003 ✓ verified · 1 run Sections are numbered, a second render gets the first's words, and auditor-only notes are removed

When "## hello" is rendered with section numbering Then it reads "## 1.1 hello" When "Spec [[1234:9.8.7.6]]." is rendered with auditor-note exclusion Then it reads "Spec." When a template lists first_pass_output.words after the words apple and banana, rendered with the vocabulary extension Then its second render reads "[apple][banana]" When numbering and note exclusion run together Then code in fenced blocks, tildes and inline code is left exactly as written, its "# a comment" unnumbered and its "[[1, 2]]" kept And only ATX headings are numbered: "#hashtag" and a lone "#" stay, "# Top" and "## Sub" become "# 1 Top" and "## 1.1 Sub" And a note over two lines of a paragraph, or nested in another, is removed whole: "A [[auditor" "only]] B." reads "A B." And a code fence inside a blockquote or a list item is code too, its notes kept And a note still open at the paragraph's end, "Stray [[ here", is kept as text

Covers: guarantee MarkdownPostProcessed · need publishing/compile-dhf

Rule: Code snippets are extracted from source files for inclusion in documents

item-07-004 ✓ verified · 1 run The lines between RDOC and ENDRDOC are a snippet under its key

When the lines "RDOC greeting", "hello", "world", "ENDRDOC" are collected Then the snippet greeting is "hello" then "world" And lines with no markers give no snippets And a marker is a whole word: "PRDOC_LIMIT = 3" starts no snippet, and the snippet limit is "LIMIT = PRDOC_LIMIT" When a.py and b.py both hold a snippet keyed "key" Then collecting them is refused, naming both files And rdm collect exits with status 2, naming b.py

Covers: guarantee SnippetsFromSource · need publishing/compile-dhf

Rule: RDM's user manual is one controlled document, published per release, that discloses every risk

item-07-005 ✓ verified · 1 run IFU-001 lists the manual's pages in the reading order of instructions for use, behind a cover

Given the controlled document IFU-001 and the pages it lists Then its chapters appear in this order: "RDM documentation", "What RDM is for", "How it works", "Limits and risks", "Install", "Quick start", "Guides", "Troubleshooting", "Reference", "Changelog" And every other page sits in the folder of the chapter page before it And the site's Docs tab shows exactly these pages, in this order And the first page is the cover, naming the product, "development version (after v1.1.0)", and "IFU-001, revision" with the manual's revision When the docs are built for the release tag v9.1.0 Then "development version (after v1.1.0) @main" reads "v9.1.0 @v9.1.0" When they are built for the development version Then it reads "development version" and the install ref "@main" And no page pins a release by hand

Covers: guarantee ManualInReadingOrder · need publishing/user-manual

item-07-006 ✓ verified · 1 run The manual is published once per release tag and once for the development version

Given the docs workflow and the site's configuration Then a release tag "v*" and a push to main both publish And a tag publishes under its own name and as latest, main as the version dev And every published version is kept on one branch, never replaced, and selectable And the newest release, latest, is the default

Covers: guarantee PublishedPerRelease · need publishing/user-manual

item-07-007 ✓ verified · 1 run The manual's "Limits and risks" chapter discloses every risk of the register by its id

Given RDM's risk register and the manual's "Limits and risks" chapter Then the chapter's risk table names every risk of the register by its id, and no other And each row says what the user must do about the residual risk

Covers: guarantee RisksDisclosedById · need publishing/user-manual

Rule: The device-master-record index and the verification report are generated from the record

item-07-008 ✓ verified · 1 run The DMR index has one entry per controlled document, from its frontmatter

Given documents/sop.md with id SOP-1, revision 2, title "The SOP" And documents/plan.md with id PLAN-1, revision 1, title "The Plan" And documents/notes.md with no frontmatter When the DMR index data is generated Then it lists PLAN-1 "The Plan" documents/plan.md revision 1, then SOP-1 "The SOP" documents/sop.md revision 2 And notes.md is named as skipped When the only documents have a blank id or an empty one Then nothing is indexed, a.md is named, and generation exits with status 1 And the output is marked GENERATED, and generating it again gives the same file

Covers: guarantee DmrIndexFromFrontmatter · need release/release-evidence

item-07-009 ✓ verified · 2 runs The verification report shows a reviewer who did not run the tests what was verified

Given a record with requirements, risks and Allure results of passing, failing and skipped runs with steps and attachments When the verification report is written Then its header names the repository, the record's commit, the commits tested, the executor and environment, the RDM version and one SHA-256 over the result files And the evidence is release-grade only when every requirement passed at the product's commit with a clean worktree; otherwise each reason is named And its anomalies list failed and skipped runs, requirements with no run, missing attachments and orphan tags And its traceability lists each requirement in spec order with its user needs, the risks it is a control for and its tests And each requirement is a baseline or a risk-based acceptance criterion, each risk shows its status and residual decision, and the register's state is summarised And each run shows its test's file and function, result, date and duration, failure message and trace And it leaves out the labels it already shows, runner internals and Allure's links And each step is a verification step, nested, with its own result And attachments show text inline up to a limit and images embedded, other files listed, the captured output and the copy of the requirement listed by SHA-256 only And the PDF shows all of it in that order, and an appendix lists every result file with its SHA-256 And text from a test reaches the page as text: markup in it is shown, not run And without the typst package a typst executable is used, and with neither the report says so And the evidence bundle includes the report, rdm story evidence-report writes it, and its SHA-256 can be checked from the bundle's copy of the results And a result it cannot lay out leaves the reason in the bundle, not a crash And a symbolic link among the results is never read: its attachment is missing and its file unhashed And every run counts, tagged with a declared requirement or not; an unreadable or linked result, and uncommitted changes to the record, are each a reason it is not release-grade Given a record whose spec lives in a repository of its own, and a passing run of that repository's commit When the verification report is written Then the product's commit is the spec repository's, the record's stays its own, and the header names both And the run is release-grade evidence

Covers: guarantee VerificationReportForAReviewer · need release/release-evidence

docs.title: release
docs.text:
Feature: Release

The accepted scenarios of this context: what holds a release back, how a requirement's status is traced from executed results, what a release retains, and RDM's gates for other repositories' CI. Each is stamped with an item id that is never renumbered or reused, and verified by the acceptance tests whose Allure results carry that id as a tag label.

Rule: A release is blocked until the spec is read whole and every requirement has a passing run

item-04-001 ✓ verified · 1 run The release gate passes only when every requirement has a passing run and none fails

Given a spec whose feature file stamps item-01-001 and item-01-002, both addressing the need Release When the release manager runs the release gate with no Allure results Then release is blocked, item-01-001 and item-01-002 untested When a passing run tagged item-01-001 is added Then release is blocked, naming item-01-002 and not item-01-001 When a failing run tagged item-01-002 is added Then release is blocked: item-01-002 failed When item-01-002's run passes and a failing run tagged item-01-001 is added Then release is blocked, naming item-01-001: one passing run does not outweigh a failing one When the failing run of item-01-001 is removed Then release passes When an unstamped scenario "an unstamped behaviour" is added to the feature file Then release is blocked, naming "an unstamped behaviour" When a second scenario is stamped item-01-001 instead Then release is blocked: item-01-001 is stamped twice When a feature file "broken.feature" that Gherkin cannot parse is added instead Then release is blocked, naming broken.feature And a slice of a Löyly plan whose spec.feature is missing (a link to a folder git never received) blocks release, naming the slice When the feature file holds no stamped scenario Then release is blocked: there is nothing to verify And a repository with no spec at all is blocked: no spec was found

Covers: rule ReleaseGate (success) · rule ReleaseGate (refusal 1) · rule ReleaseGate (refusal 2) · rule ReleaseGate (refusal 3) · rule ReleaseGate (refusal 4) · rule ReleaseGate (refusal 5) · rule ReleaseGate (refusal 6) · need release/release-blocked

Rule: Each requirement's status is reconciled from the tag labels of executed Allure results

item-04-002 ✓ verified · 1 run Verified, failed and untested come from the runs that carry each requirement's id

Given Allure results: run p passed tagged item-01-001, run f failed tagged item-01-002, run s skipped tagged item-01-003, run b broken tagged item-01-004 When the requirements item-01-001 to item-01-005 are reconciled against them Then item-01-001 is verified And item-01-002 and item-01-004 have failed And item-01-003 and item-01-005 are untested When a failing run names item-01-001 only as its story, feature and epic labels Then item-01-001 is still verified: only a tag label claims a requirement When a passing run carries the tag label "@item-01-005" Then item-01-005 is verified: the "@" before the id is read When item-01-001 to item-01-003 address the need Release, item-01-004 and item-01-005 the need Trace, and verify writes the verification data Then the traceability matrix rendered from it shows each requirement's status under the need it addresses

Covers: rule Verify (success) · need release/trace-verification

Rule: A release's evidence is retained as one bundle, generated from the record, never mixed with an earlier one

item-04-003 ✓ verified · 1 run The evidence bundle holds the verification data, the rendered matrix, the report and the results

Given a record with a spec, a traceability matrix template and Allure results with attachments and a container When the release manager writes the evidence bundle to an output directory apart from the results Then the bundle holds the verification data computed from the executed results And the traceability matrix rendered from it, with no template markers left And the executed results with every attachment and container they reference And the verification report, or the manifest says why it is not there And a manifest listing exactly the files bundled And a symbolic link among the results is not followed, and a missing attachment is listed in the manifest And an unreadable result is named in the manifest When the bundle is written again over the earlier one Then its results replace the earlier bundle's, never mixed with them When the output directory would hold the results or sit inside them Then the bundle is refused and the results are left untouched When the record has no traceability matrix template Then the bundle is refused, naming the missing template, and no bundle is written

Covers: rule EvidenceBundle (success) · rule EvidenceBundle (refusal 1) · rule EvidenceBundle (refusal 2) · need release/release-evidence

Rule: RDM's gates can be reused in another repository's CI, pinned to one RDM revision

item-04-004 ✓ verified · 1 run The reusable workflow and the gates action run RDM's gates at the revision the caller pins

Given the composite gates action, the reusable gates workflow and the documents action When the gates action is run with the checklist part11_document_control over a record with results Then it runs verify, the release gate, graph validation and the evidence bundle with the verification report, in that order And graph validation holds the documents to the checklists named And a gate that fails fails the action And with the release gate off and no results yet, no gate runs And every rdm command the workflow and the actions run is one RDM's command line accepts And the action installs RDM from its own revision, the workflow from the revision the caller pins, never from a package index And the reusable workflow runs the caller's acceptance tests before the gates And the documents action renders with the image of the release it is pinned to, else the latest image And the workflow rdm adopt lays down calls the reusable workflow pinned to the installed RDM's version And RDM's own CI calls the same workflow, pinned to the commit under test

Covers: guarantee GatesReusableInCi · need specification/adopt-repository

docs.title: risk
docs.text:
Feature: Risk

The accepted scenarios of this context: the risk register kept in the record, each risk scored only against the risk policy the project declares, each control a requirement of the spec, and the release held back while a risk is unscored, uncontrolled, or residually unacceptable without a named acceptance. Each is stamped with an item id that is never renumbered or reused, and verified by the acceptance tests whose Allure results carry that id as a tag label.

Rule: The register is read from kind: risk frontmatter and evaluated only against a declared policy

item-02-001 ✓ verified · 1 run Every field of a risk is read, and its levels come only from the declared risk policy

Given dhf/documents/risk/risks.md, of kind: risk and status proposed, declares RISK-A-1, RISK-A-2 and RISK-A-3 And RISK-A-1 is a security risk with STRIDE category Spoofing, linked to RISK-A-2, hazard "Hz", situation "Si", harm "Ha", scored Serious × Possible with recorded level High, controlled by item-01-001 and item-01-002, with residual probability Unlikely, accepted by "QA lead" because "ALARP", and status approved And RISK-A-2 is a safety risk scored Serious × Possible, controlled by item-01-001, with residual Minor × Possible and no status of its own And RISK-A-3 is a safety risk scored Minor × Rare that nothing controls And dhf/documents/notes.md declares a risk RISK-NOT-1 but is not of kind: risk When the register is read with no risk policy declared Then it holds RISK-A-1, RISK-A-2 and RISK-A-3 and not RISK-NOT-1 And every field of RISK-A-1 is read as written, its residual severity left unset, its document dhf/documents/risk/risks.md And RISK-A-2 has the document's status, proposed And no risk has a level or a residual level: nothing is evaluated without a policy When dhf/documents/risk/policy.md declares a risk policy with status proposed, in which Medium is acceptable only with a justification Then RISK-A-1 is High, residual Medium: its residual severity defaults to the initial Serious And RISK-A-2 is High, residual Medium, from its own residual Minor × Possible And RISK-A-3, uncontrolled, is Low and residual Low When the policy names its own levels Green, Amber and Red and a risk scored Bad × Often has residual probability Seldom Then that risk is Red, residual Amber When the policy gives no acceptability, leaves a severity and probability pair without a level, calls a level "fine", or lists a severity or probability twice Then the policy is refused, naming documents/risk/policy.md When a second document, documents/risk/second_policy.md, also declares a risk policy Then the policy is refused, naming both documents

Covers: guarantee RegisterReadFromFrontmatter · need risk/risk-register

Rule: The release gate blocks a register it cannot evaluate as written

item-02-002 ✓ verified · 1 run A register or policy that cannot be evaluated as written blocks release, naming the risk or the document

Given a spec whose requirement item-01-001 has a passing run and item-01-002 none And in the record: \<register> When the release manager runs the release gate Then its risk findings are \<findings> And each finding about one risk names that risk

Examples: the register's own rules

case register findings sound the risk policy is declared; five sound risks, one a security risk of STRIDE category Tampering linked to another, two accepted by "QA lead" because "ALARP", one whose control lowers the residual severity none no-policy no risk policy is declared; RISK-P-1 "the risk register has risks but no risk_policy is declared (acceptability criteria missing)" and "risk RISK-P-1 cannot be evaluated: no risk policy" duplicate the risk policy is declared; RISK-D-1 declared twice "risk RISK-D-1 is declared 2 times" no-hazard the risk policy is declared; RISK-C-1 with an empty hazard "risk RISK-C-1 has no hazard" no-situation the risk policy is declared; RISK-C-2 with no situation "risk RISK-C-2 has no situation" no-harm the risk policy is declared; RISK-C-3 whose harm is blank "risk RISK-C-3 has no harm" untyped-parts the risk policy is declared; RISK-C-4 whose hazard, situation and harm are not text "risk RISK-C-4 has no hazard", "risk RISK-C-4 has no situation" and "risk RISK-C-4 has no harm" no-category the risk policy is declared; RISK-B-1 with no category one, naming RISK-B-1, that "needs a category of safety or security" bad-category the risk policy is declared; RISK-B-2 of category ops one, naming RISK-B-2, that "needs a category of safety or security (got ops)" no-stride the risk policy is declared; RISK-B-3, a security risk with no STRIDE category one, naming RISK-B-3, that "is a security risk with no STRIDE category" bad-stride the risk policy is declared; RISK-B-4, a security risk of STRIDE category Hacking one, naming RISK-B-4, with "no STRIDE category" bad-link the risk policy is declared; RISK-B-5 linked to RISK-NOPE-9 "risk RISK-B-5 links RISK-NOPE-9, which is not a declared risk" unknown-severity the risk policy is declared; RISK-S-1 of severity Awful one, naming RISK-S-1, that "is not defined by the risk policy" unknown-probability the risk policy is declared; RISK-S-2 with no probability one, naming RISK-S-2, that "is not defined by the risk policy" mis-scored the risk policy is declared; RISK-S-3, Serious × Possible, recording level Low "risk RISK-S-3 records level Low; the risk policy says High" mis-scored-residual the risk policy is declared; RISK-S-4, residual probability Rare, recording residual level Block "risk RISK-S-4 records residual level Block; the risk policy says Low" scalar-control the risk policy is declared; RISK-U-5 with the single control item-01-077 and the single link RISK-NOPE-9 "risk RISK-U-5 names control item-01-077, which is not a requirement of the spec" and "risk RISK-U-5 links RISK-NOPE-9, which is not a declared risk" undeclared-control the risk policy is declared; RISK-U-2 controlled by item-01-001 and item-01-077 "risk RISK-U-2 names control item-01-077, which is not a requirement of the spec" no-residual the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-1 with controls and no residual "risk RISK-R-1 has controls but no residual score" bad-residual the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-2 with residual probability Never one, naming RISK-R-2, that "residual 'Serious' × 'Never' is not defined" no-register no risk document at all, and no risk policy none: the policy is required only when there are risks anonymous the risk policy is declared; a risk with no id "a risk in dhf/documents/risk/risks.md has no id" malformed-policy documents/risk/policy.md declares risk_policy: [1, 2]; a risk one naming "risk_policy in documents/risk/policy.md" policy-twice the risk policy is declared in documents/risk/policy.md and again in documents/risk/second_policy.md; a risk one that "risk_policy is declared twice", naming second_policy.md risks-a-mapping the risk policy is declared; a document of kind: risk whose risks are a mapping of id to risk release blocked, naming documents/risk/risks.md risks-strings the risk policy is declared; a document of kind: risk whose risks are the string RISK-M-2 release blocked, naming documents/risk/risks.md risks-misspelled the risk policy is declared; a document of kind: risk that lists its risks under risk: release blocked, naming documents/risk/risks.md no-risks the risk policy is declared; a document of kind: risk with no risks release blocked, naming documents/risk/risks.md capital-kind the risk policy is declared; a document of kind: Risk whose RISK-M-3, Critical × Likely, nothing controls release blocked, naming RISK-M-3: its kind is read in any case policy-only a document of kind: risk that only declares the approved risk policy; item-01-001 and item-01-002 pass none, and release passes: it is not a register list-id the risk policy is declared; a risk whose id is the list [RISK-I-1], and RISK-I-1 "a risk in dhf/documents/risk/risks.md has an id that is not text or a number: ['RISK-I-1']" numeric-severities a policy whose severities are the numbers 1 and 2; RISK-N-1 of severity 2 × Likely, residual Rare; item-01-001 and item-01-002 pass none, and release passes

Covers: guarantee MalformedRegisterBlocks · need risk/risk-register

Rule: A risk is released only with an evaluated, acceptable or accepted residual and a known status

item-02-003 ✓ verified · 1 run An unevaluated, unacceptable or unaccepted residual blocks release; a proposed rating only warns

Given a spec whose requirement item-01-001 has a passing run and item-01-002 none And in the record: \<register> When the release manager runs the release gate Then its risk findings are \<findings>

Examples: the residual decision and the status

case register findings unverified-control the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-6 controlled by item-01-001 and item-01-002, which has no passing run "risk RISK-R-6: residual not evaluated — control item-01-002 has no passing test" uncontrolled-unacceptable the risk policy is declared; RISK-U-1, Critical × Likely, that nothing controls, accepted by "QA lead" because "ALARP" "risk RISK-U-1 has an unacceptable residual level of Block": no acceptance makes Block pass uncontrolled-claimed-residual the risk policy is declared; RISK-U-4, Critical × Likely, that nothing controls, claiming residual Negligible × Rare "risk RISK-U-4 has an unacceptable residual level of Block": only a control reduces a risk uncontrolled-unaccepted the risk policy is declared; RISK-U-3, Serious × Unlikely, that nothing controls, with no acceptance one, naming RISK-U-3, that "has a residual level of Medium that needs an acceptance" block-residual the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-3, Critical × Likely, residual probability Likely, accepted "risk RISK-R-3 has an unacceptable residual level of Block" unaccepted-medium the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-4 with residual probability Unlikely and no acceptance one, naming RISK-R-4, that "has a residual level of Medium that needs an acceptance" half-accepted-high the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-5 with residual probability Possible, accepted by "QA" with no reason one, naming RISK-R-5, that "has a residual level of High that needs an acceptance" acceptance-not-text the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-7 with residual probability Unlikely, accepted by an empty list because "ALARP" one, naming RISK-R-7, that "has a residual level of Medium that needs an acceptance" acceptance-not-words the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-8 with residual probability Unlikely, accepted by "QA lead" because true one, naming RISK-R-8, that "has a residual level of Medium that needs an acceptance" bad-status the risk policy is declared; RISK-T-1 of status maybe "risk RISK-T-1 has an unknown status 'maybe' (proposed or approved)" proposed the risk policy, of status proposed; RISK-W-1 of status proposed and RISK-W-2 approved; item-01-001 and item-01-002 pass none, and release passes, warning "risk RISK-W-1 is proposed: a person has not approved its rating" and "the risk policy in documents/risk/policy.md is proposed: a person has not approved it", and nothing about RISK-W-2 no-status the risk policy, with no status; RISK-W-3 of empty status and RISK-W-4 with none; item-01-001 and item-01-002 pass none, and release passes, warning that RISK-W-3, RISK-W-4 and the risk policy are proposed: no status is never approved

Covers: guarantee UncontrolledRiskBlocks · need risk/risk-register

docs.title: specification
docs.text:
Feature: Specification

The accepted scenarios of this context: how RDM reads the spec it holds a record to (its requirements and the user needs they address), how a project is scaffolded or an existing repository adopted, and how validation by a person shows at release. Each is stamped with an item id that is never renumbered or reused, and verified by the acceptance tests whose Allure results carry that id as a tag label.

Rule: The spec's requirements are its Gherkin scenarios tagged with an id, read whole and never dropped quietly

item-01-001 ✓ verified · 2 runs Every tagged scenario is a requirement, wherever the spec's layout keeps it

Given a Löyly plan whose slices are 03-gate, 04-stamps, 05-later with status planned and 06-someday with status backlog And 03-gate's spec.feature holds, under the Rule "Booting", a scenario "boots fresh" tagged @allium-rule-success.BootFresh @allium-guarantee.Fresh @item-03-001, a scenario " refuses a busy seam" tagged @item-03-009 @item-03-002, and an untagged scenario "has no stamp" And 03-gate has a drafts.feature, and an entry "notes" that is no slice holds a spec.feature When the spec is read Then its requirements are item-03-001, item-03-002 and item-04-001, in plan order, in the contexts gate and stamps And 05-later and 06-someday are skipped and recorded as planned and backlog, and the drafts and "notes" are never read And item-03-001 keeps its Rule "Booting", its title and its source line ".pi/plan/03-gate/spec.feature:6" And the second scenario's id is item-03-002, the last of its item tags, and its title is trimmed to "refuses a busy seam" And item-04-001 has no Rule: a Rule never carries over from another file And item-03-001's Allium obligations are rule-success BootFresh and guarantee Fresh And "has no stamp" is listed as unstamped at ".pi/plan/03-gate/spec.feature:14", and no id is stamped twice And reading the spec imports no planning tool And Löyly's own spec, when present, reads as its checklist golden: 201 stamped items, per context Given instead a repository with no spec configuration and feature files under features/ And features/alarms/sound.feature holds, under the Rule "Thresholds", a scenario "a high heart rate alarms" tagged @smoke @REQ-1, and an untagged scenario "not yet tagged" And features/top.feature holds a scenario "at the root" tagged @REQ-2 When the spec is read Then features/ is found, and REQ-1 and REQ-2 are its requirements: any id-shaped tag is an id And REQ-1 is in the context alarms, under the Feature "Alarms sound" and the Rule "Thresholds", sourced at features/alarms/sound.feature:7, keeping the tag @smoke And REQ-2, at the root, has no context And "not yet tagged" is listed as unstamped at features/alarms/sound.feature:10 When the configuration names the globs "../features/**/*.feature", excludes "top.feature" and sets the id pattern "REQ-1" Then the only requirement is REQ-1

Covers: guarantee SpecReadAsTaggedGherkin · need publishing/compile-dhf

Rule: A project starts from one command, and an existing repository is adopted without disturbing it

item-01-002 ✓ verified · 1 run rdm init scaffolds a project that builds offline, and refuses a directory that exists

docs.text:
Feature: Test evidence

The accepted scenarios of this context: how executed Allure results are read as test runs, and what an acceptance run records about the version it tested and who ran it. Each is stamped with an item id that is never renumbered or reused, and verified by the acceptance tests whose Allure results carry that id as a tag label.

Rule: A result RDM cannot read is never counted as a pass

item-03-001 ✓ verified · 1 run An unreadable result blocks release and is named, and a failed step fails its run

Given a spec whose only requirement is item-01-001, addressing the need Release And a passing Allure result "a" tagged item-01-001 Then the release gate passes When a result "b" is added that cannot be read, holding any of:

content JSON cut short after '"value": "item-01-001"' a JSON list, not an object bytes that are not UTF-8

Then release is blocked: the result is unreadable, and it could hold a failed run When result "b" is a failed run tagged item-01-001 written with a byte-order mark Then it is read, and release is blocked: item-01-001 failed When a result "b" tagged item-01-001, beside the passing result "a", has any of:

case what is wrong capital-status the status "Failed", which Allure does not write no-status no status null-status a null status labels-text labels given as the text "tag=item-01-001" tag-list a tag label whose value is a list link it is a symbolic link to a result elsewhere deep JSON nested 100000 levels deep

Then release is blocked by that unreadable result alone When failing runs beside the passing result "a" are tagged "Item-01-001", "item_01_001", "item–01-001" and "item-01-777" Then release passes, and the gate warns "Allure result tag \<tag> matches no requirement" for each of the four When a run marked passed has an inner step that failed, and another an inner step that broke Then both runs have failed, and so have the requirements they claim When a result "x-result.json" cannot be read and verify is run Then verify exits non-zero and the verification data lists x-result.json as unreadable

docs.title: Assurance activities
docs.text:
Proportionate to that risk ([[CSA:assurance]]):

  • Scripted, automated testing. Each of RDM's 44 requirements (stamped Given/When/Then scenarios in .pi/spec/) is verified by an acceptance test that claims it; RDM's own release gate blocks while any requirement lacks a passing run, any user need is unaddressed, or any risk control is unverified.
  • Risk-based focus. The requirements that control one of the risks (the release gate, the read-only agent server, the served graph) count only once verified and the risk's residual is evaluated again.
  • Scenario testing on a real product. The worked example runs RDM's gates over Löyly's pi harness (201 requirements, six clojure.test suites, a spec in another repository) on every change to RDM, beside RDM's own record.
  • Ongoing monitoring. Every change runs every gate in CI, on RDM's own record (dogfooding) and on the example; a gate that stops passing stops the change.

The assurance also relies on ([[CSA:assurance-considerations]]): the dependencies pinned in uv.lock, the RDM container image built from them, and the executed results RDM keeps as evidence rather than screenshots.

docs.title: Record
docs.text: The record of each validation ([[CSA:record]], [[13485:4.1.6-records]]) is the evidence bundle the design-controls workflow writes from each run: the verification report (the commit validated, who and what ran the tests and where, each requirement with its runs, the issues found, and whether the evidence is release-grade), the traceability matrix, the verification data and the results with a manifest and one SHA-256 over them. The conclusion is the release gate's verdict; the approval, the reviewed pull request.

docs.title: The record system and Part 11
docs.text: The validation record is required as evidence of a validated state and is kept electronically, so it is a Part 11 electronic record and the system that keeps it is held to Part 11 ([[CSA:part11]]): git as the document control system, GitHub as its service provider and RDM's gates, mapped control by control in DC-001. That system is validated by this same procedure: RDM's gates are what the assurance above tests.

docs.title: Change
docs.text: RDM is validated before a release is first used and again after every change ([[13485:4.1.6-before-use]], [[CSA:change]]): every pull request runs every gate before it can merge; a release is a tag, and a team adopting RDM pins its CI to one release (the reusable workflow and the image, item-04-004), so a new RDM release reaches a team only when it changes the pin, and the team assesses that change for its own use ([[13485:7.5.6-software]] where RDM is used in production).

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: RDM's instructions for use (IFU) are its user manual, the documentation site: what anyone who uses RDM follows to keep a record the way RDM's gates enforce. It is a design output, and this controlled document is its entry in the device-master-record index (rdm story dmr): the pages listed above, at the revision of the release they ship with.

docs.title: How it is controlled
docs.text:
• Approval: each change to a page is a reviewed pull request; the release tag fixes the version that ships.
  • Requirements: what the manual must hold is stated as requirements of the publishing context (item-07-005, item-07-006, item-07-007), verified like any other.
  • Changing this list: adding or removing a page changes this document, so its revision is bumped.

docs.title: Verification and Validation Plan — RDM
docs.text: Id: VVP-001 · Download as PDF

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text: Defines how RDM is verified (does it meet its requirements, the acceptance criteria?) and validated (does it meet the user needs / intended use?). The vocabulary is the repository's CONTEXT.md.

docs.title: Intended use
docs.text: RDM audits the record of regulated software — the spec it is held to (in Gherkin), checklists, risks, test results and their git history — and lets the team gate releases on it, check documents against standards, render regulatory documents from it, and query it as a read-only graph. Its users are regulatory authors, engineers, reviewers, and agents working under their direction. RDM is not a medical device and does not itself establish compliance; it keeps the evidence that a team presents.

docs.title: User needs
docs.text: RDM's user needs are in its spec, written the Löyly way: each is a screen of a context's event model (.pi/spec/<context>/event-model/area.edn), its key the need's id (release/release-blocked) and its description what the actor needs, linked to the Allium surface that models it (who it faces, the rules it provides, what it guarantees) and to the event-storm events behind it. They are the validation anchors. Every user need must be addressed by a verified requirement before a release, and validated by a person: a validation record in dhf/validation/ names the need's id.

docs.title: Verification approach
docs.text: RDM's requirements are the accepted scenarios of its spec (.pi/spec/<context>/spec.feature, one directory per bounded context, each a slice of .pi/plan/), each a concrete Given/When/Then example stamped @item-NN-SSS and tagged with the Allium rule or guarantee it covers, which links it to the user need it addresses. Each is an acceptance criterion, verified by the automated tests in RDM's tests/acceptance/ that claim it with @allure.tag("item-NN-SSS"). The test's verification steps are its own, not criteria: a requirement is accepted as a whole. A user need is met when it is validated and every requirement addressing it is verified; a requirement that is a risk control counts once it is verified and its risk's residual is acceptable. rdm story release-gate enforces this.

docs.title: Validation approach
docs.text:
User need Summative (record of truth) Formative (supporting) publishing/compile-dhf; release/release-blocked; release/trace-verification maintainer review that the compiled DHF, gates, and traceability meet the documented intent dogfooding: RDM compiles its own DHF (this file set) specification/validation-visible maintainer review that the release gate names every user need without an approved validation record dogfooding: RDM's own release gate warns on its unvalidated needs compliance/gap-analysis maintainer review that gap analysis flags real missing standard references against shipped checklists dogfooding: rdm gap over RDM's own released docs specification/scaffold-project maintainer review that a scaffolded project builds a release and passes the relevant gap checklists dogfooding: fresh_release_test builds an init'd project end-to-end specification/adopt-repository maintainer review that an adopted repository ends up with the DHF skeleton and the CI gates and that nothing pre-existing was overwritten trial adoption into a scratch copy of a real repository; rdm adopt acceptance test exercises the skip-not-overwrite contract release/release-evidence maintainer review that a produced evidence bundle and DMR index are complete and agree with the record they were generated from dogfooding: rdm story dmr / evidence-bundle run against RDM's own DHF graph/explore-graph maintainer review that the projected graph agrees with the record it was built from (the spec's needs and requirements, contexts, documents, results, commits) and is explorable in a graph browser dogfooding: RDM's own DHF projected, queried, and browsed in AWS Graph Explorer graph/agent-reads-record maintainer review that an agent harness connected to the server answers traceability questions about RDM's own record correctly and has no way to change it dogfooding: agent sessions on RDM itself using rdm graph mcp risk/risk-register maintainer review that the gate's risk findings match a manual review of the same register with the risk-analysis method dogfooding: RDM's own tool-risk register (in CSV-001, dhf/documents/tool_validation.md) held to the release gate publishing/user-manual maintainer review that the manual's pages teach what the gates enforce dogfooding: RDM's own manual (dhf/documents/user_manual.md), published per release

Formative evidence never gates release.

    root: String
}

entity Project {
    directory: String
    templates: List<String>
}

-- An existing repository brought under RDM by rdm adopt.
entity Adoption {
    repository: String
    laid_down: List<String>
    skipped: List<String>
}

-- A person's validation of one user need: dhf/validation/<name>-validation.json.
entity ValidationRecord {
    user_need: UserNeed
    disposition: String
    reviewer: String
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Rules
------------------------------------------------------------

-- Scaffold a new documentation project from the shipped templates.
rule Init {
    when: Init(author, directory)
    -- 1. the directory does not yet exist: init never writes into an existing one
    requires: not exists directory
    ensures:
        Project.created(directory: directory)
        -- with a spec skeleton written the Löyly way: one slice, one context, one need
        SpecSkeleton.created(root: directory)
        ProjectScaffolded(directory: directory)
}

-- Bring an existing repository under RDM: the DHF skeleton, the CI gate workflow and a
-- .gitignore of what RDM generates. A destination that exists, a symbolic link
-- included, is skipped and reported, never overwritten or written through.
rule Adopt {
    when: Adopt(author, repository)
    ensures:
        Adoption.created(repository: repository)
        -- a repository that keeps a spec keeps it; one with none gets the skeleton
        if not has_spec(repository): SpecSkeleton.created(root: repository)
        RepositoryAdopted(repository: repository)
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Actor Declarations
------------------------------------------------------------

actor RegulatoryAuthor {
    identified_by: AuthorAccount where true
}

actor Reviewer {
    identified_by: ReviewerAccount where true
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Surfaces
------------------------------------------------------------

-- A regulatory author can scaffold a new compliant documentation project from a single
-- command.
surface ScaffoldProject {
    facing author: RegulatoryAuthor
    context project: Project

    provides:
        Init(author, directory)
}

-- An existing repository can be brought under RDM from a single command, without
-- disturbing its current contents.
surface AdoptRepository {
    facing author: RegulatoryAuthor
    context adoption: Adoption

    provides:
        Adopt(author, repository)

    @guarantee GatesReusableInCi
        -- RDM's gates run in the adopted repository's CI from RDM's reusable workflow and
        -- actions, installed from the one RDM revision the caller pins.
}

-- A reviewer can see, at release, which user needs have no approved validation by a
-- person.
surface ValidationAtRelease {
    facing reviewer: Reviewer
    context record: ValidationRecord

    exposes:
        record.user_need
        record.disposition
        record.reviewer

    @guarantee UnvalidatedNeedsNamedAtRelease
        -- The release gate names, as a warning that never blocks, each user need with no
        -- approved validation record naming its reviewer.
}
