docs.title: risk/risk-register
docs.text:
A team can keep its risk register in the record, each risk scored from its own matrix and each control a verified requirement, and cannot release while a risk is unscored, uncontrolled, or residually unacceptable without a named acceptance.

  • Surface: RiskRegisterDesk
  • Facing: RiskOwner
  • Guarantees: MalformedRegisterBlocks, RegisterReadFromFrontmatter, RisksProjectedWithShapes, UncontrolledRiskBlocks

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Requirement Scenario Addresses Rule item-02-001 Every field of a risk is read, and its levels come only from the declared risk policy risk/risk-register The register is read from kind: risk frontmatter and evaluated only against a declared policy item-02-002 A register or policy that cannot be evaluated as written blocks release, naming the risk or the document risk/risk-register The release gate blocks a register it cannot evaluate as written item-02-003 An unevaluated, unacceptable or unaccepted residual blocks release; a proposed rating only warns risk/risk-register A risk is released only with an evaluated, acceptable or accepted residual and a known status spec.feature 
Feature: Risk
  The accepted scenarios of this context: the risk register kept in the
  record, each risk scored only against the risk policy the project declares,
  each control a requirement of the spec, and the release held back while a
  risk is unscored, uncontrolled, or residually unacceptable without a named
  acceptance. Each is stamped with an item id that is never renumbered or
  reused, and verified by the acceptance tests whose Allure results carry
  that id as a tag label.

  Rule: The register is read from kind: risk frontmatter and evaluated only against a declared policy

    # risk.allium, surface RiskRegisterDesk, guarantee RegisterReadFromFrontmatter
    @allium-guarantee.RegisterReadFromFrontmatter
    @item-02-001
    Scenario: Every field of a risk is read, and its levels come only from the declared risk policy
      Given dhf/documents/risk/risks.md, of kind: risk and status proposed, declares RISK-A-1, RISK-A-2 and RISK-A-3
      And RISK-A-1 is a security risk with STRIDE category Spoofing, linked to RISK-A-2, hazard "Hz", situation "Si", harm "Ha", scored Serious × Possible with recorded level High, controlled by item-01-001 and item-01-002, with residual probability Unlikely, accepted by "QA lead" because "ALARP", and status approved
      And RISK-A-2 is a safety risk scored Serious × Possible, controlled by item-01-001, with residual Minor × Possible and no status of its own
      And RISK-A-3 is a safety risk scored Minor × Rare that nothing controls
      And dhf/documents/notes.md declares a risk RISK-NOT-1 but is not of kind: risk
      When the register is read with no risk policy declared
      Then it holds RISK-A-1, RISK-A-2 and RISK-A-3 and not RISK-NOT-1
      And every field of RISK-A-1 is read as written, its residual severity left unset, its document dhf/documents/risk/risks.md
      And RISK-A-2 has the document's status, proposed
      And no risk has a level or a residual level: nothing is evaluated without a policy
      When dhf/documents/risk/policy.md declares a risk policy with status proposed, in which Medium is acceptable only with a justification
      Then RISK-A-1 is High, residual Medium: its residual severity defaults to the initial Serious
      And RISK-A-2 is High, residual Medium, from its own residual Minor × Possible
      And RISK-A-3, uncontrolled, is Low and residual Low
      When the policy names its own levels Green, Amber and Red and a risk scored Bad × Often has residual probability Seldom
      Then that risk is Red, residual Amber
      When the policy gives no acceptability, leaves a severity and probability pair without a level, calls a level "fine", or lists a severity or probability twice
      Then the policy is refused, naming documents/risk/policy.md
      When a second document, documents/risk/second_policy.md, also declares a risk policy
      Then the policy is refused, naming both documents

  Rule: The release gate blocks a register it cannot evaluate as written

    # risk.allium, surface RiskRegisterDesk, guarantee MalformedRegisterBlocks
    @allium-guarantee.MalformedRegisterBlocks
    @item-02-002
    Scenario Outline: A register or policy that cannot be evaluated as written blocks release, naming the risk or the document
      Given a spec whose requirement item-01-001 has a passing run and item-01-002 none
      And in the record: <register>
      When the release manager runs the release gate
      Then its risk findings are <findings>
      And each finding about one risk names that risk

      Examples: the register's own rules
        | case                | register                                                                                                                                                                                                     | findings                                                                                                                                              |
        | sound               | the risk policy is declared; five sound risks, one a security risk of STRIDE category Tampering linked to another, two accepted by "QA lead" because "ALARP", one whose control lowers the residual severity | none                                                                                                                                                  |
        | no-policy           | no risk policy is declared; RISK-P-1                                                                                                                                                                         | "the risk register has risks but no risk_policy is declared (acceptability criteria missing)" and "risk RISK-P-1 cannot be evaluated: no risk policy" |
        | duplicate           | the risk policy is declared; RISK-D-1 declared twice                                                                                                                                                         | "risk RISK-D-1 is declared 2 times"                                                                                                                   |
        | no-hazard           | the risk policy is declared; RISK-C-1 with an empty hazard                                                                                                                                                   | "risk RISK-C-1 has no hazard"                                                                                                                         |
        | no-situation        | the risk policy is declared; RISK-C-2 with no situation                                                                                                                                                      | "risk RISK-C-2 has no situation"                                                                                                                      |
        | no-harm             | the risk policy is declared; RISK-C-3 whose harm is blank                                                                                                                                                    | "risk RISK-C-3 has no harm"                                                                                                                           |
        | untyped-parts       | the risk policy is declared; RISK-C-4 whose hazard, situation and harm are not text                                                                                                                          | "risk RISK-C-4 has no hazard", "risk RISK-C-4 has no situation" and "risk RISK-C-4 has no harm"                                                       |
        | no-category         | the risk policy is declared; RISK-B-1 with no category                                                                                                                                                       | one, naming RISK-B-1, that "needs a category of safety or security"                                                                                   |
        | bad-category        | the risk policy is declared; RISK-B-2 of category ops                                                                                                                                                        | one, naming RISK-B-2, that "needs a category of safety or security (got ops)"                                                                         |
        | no-stride           | the risk policy is declared; RISK-B-3, a security risk with no STRIDE category                                                                                                                               | one, naming RISK-B-3, that "is a security risk with no STRIDE category"                                                                               |
        | bad-stride          | the risk policy is declared; RISK-B-4, a security risk of STRIDE category Hacking                                                                                                                            | one, naming RISK-B-4, with "no STRIDE category"                                                                                                       |
        | bad-link            | the risk policy is declared; RISK-B-5 linked to RISK-NOPE-9                                                                                                                                                  | "risk RISK-B-5 links RISK-NOPE-9, which is not a declared risk"                                                                                       |
        | unknown-severity    | the risk policy is declared; RISK-S-1 of severity Awful                                                                                                                                                      | one, naming RISK-S-1, that "is not defined by the risk policy"                                                                                        |
        | unknown-probability | the risk policy is declared; RISK-S-2 with no probability                                                                                                                                                    | one, naming RISK-S-2, that "is not defined by the risk policy"                                                                                        |
        | mis-scored          | the risk policy is declared; RISK-S-3, Serious × Possible, recording level Low                                                                                                                               | "risk RISK-S-3 records level Low; the risk policy says High"                                                                                          |
        | mis-scored-residual | the risk policy is declared; RISK-S-4, residual probability Rare, recording residual level Block                                                                                                             | "risk RISK-S-4 records residual level Block; the risk policy says Low"                                                                                |
        | scalar-control      | the risk policy is declared; RISK-U-5 with the single control item-01-077 and the single link RISK-NOPE-9                                                                                                    | "risk RISK-U-5 names control item-01-077, which is not a requirement of the spec" and "risk RISK-U-5 links RISK-NOPE-9, which is not a declared risk" |
        | undeclared-control  | the risk policy is declared; RISK-U-2 controlled by item-01-001 and item-01-077                                                                                                                              | "risk RISK-U-2 names control item-01-077, which is not a requirement of the spec"                                                                     |
        | no-residual         | the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-1 with controls and no residual                                                                                                                                          | "risk RISK-R-1 has controls but no residual score"                                                                                                    |
        | bad-residual        | the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-2 with residual probability Never                                                                                                                                        | one, naming RISK-R-2, that "residual 'Serious' × 'Never' is not defined"                                                                              |
        | no-register         | no risk document at all, and no risk policy                                                                                                                                                                  | none: the policy is required only when there are risks                                                                                                |
        | anonymous           | the risk policy is declared; a risk with no id                                                                                                                                                               | "a risk in dhf/documents/risk/risks.md has no id"                                                                                                     |
        | malformed-policy    | documents/risk/policy.md declares risk_policy: [1, 2]; a risk                                                                                                                                                | one naming "risk_policy in documents/risk/policy.md"                                                                                                  |
        | policy-twice        | the risk policy is declared in documents/risk/policy.md and again in documents/risk/second_policy.md; a risk                                                                                                 | one that "risk_policy is declared twice", naming second_policy.md                                                                                     |
        | risks-a-mapping     | the risk policy is declared; a document of kind: risk whose risks are a mapping of id to risk                                                                                                                | release blocked, naming documents/risk/risks.md                                                                                                       |
        | risks-strings       | the risk policy is declared; a document of kind: risk whose risks are the string RISK-M-2                                                                                                                    | release blocked, naming documents/risk/risks.md                                                                                                       |
        | risks-misspelled    | the risk policy is declared; a document of kind: risk that lists its risks under risk:                                                                                                                       | release blocked, naming documents/risk/risks.md                                                                                                       |
        | no-risks            | the risk policy is declared; a document of kind: risk with no risks                                                                                                                                          | release blocked, naming documents/risk/risks.md                                                                                                       |
        | capital-kind        | the risk policy is declared; a document of kind: Risk whose RISK-M-3, Critical × Likely, nothing controls                                                                                                    | release blocked, naming RISK-M-3: its kind is read in any case                                                                                        |
        | policy-only         | a document of kind: risk that only declares the approved risk policy; item-01-001 and item-01-002 pass                                                                                                       | none, and release passes: it is not a register                                                                                                        |
        | list-id             | the risk policy is declared; a risk whose id is the list [RISK-I-1], and RISK-I-1                                                                                                                            | "a risk in dhf/documents/risk/risks.md has an id that is not text or a number: ['RISK-I-1']"                                                          |
        | numeric-severities  | a policy whose severities are the numbers 1 and 2; RISK-N-1 of severity 2 × Likely, residual Rare; item-01-001 and item-01-002 pass                                                                          | none, and release passes                                                                                                                              |

  Rule: A risk is released only with an evaluated, acceptable or accepted residual and a known status

    # risk.allium, surface RiskRegisterDesk, guarantee UncontrolledRiskBlocks
    @allium-guarantee.UncontrolledRiskBlocks
    @item-02-003
    Scenario Outline: An unevaluated, unacceptable or unaccepted residual blocks release; a proposed rating only warns
      Given a spec whose requirement item-01-001 has a passing run and item-01-002 none
      And in the record: <register>
      When the release manager runs the release gate
      Then its risk findings are <findings>

      Examples: the residual decision and the status
        | case                          | register                                                                                                                 | findings                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
        | unverified-control            | the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-6 controlled by item-01-001 and item-01-002, which has no passing run                | "risk RISK-R-6: residual not evaluated — control item-01-002 has no passing test"                                                                                                                                           |
        | uncontrolled-unacceptable     | the risk policy is declared; RISK-U-1, Critical × Likely, that nothing controls, accepted by "QA lead" because "ALARP"   | "risk RISK-U-1 has an unacceptable residual level of Block": no acceptance makes Block pass                                                                                                                                 |
        | uncontrolled-claimed-residual | the risk policy is declared; RISK-U-4, Critical × Likely, that nothing controls, claiming residual Negligible × Rare     | "risk RISK-U-4 has an unacceptable residual level of Block": only a control reduces a risk                                                                                                                                  |
        | uncontrolled-unaccepted       | the risk policy is declared; RISK-U-3, Serious × Unlikely, that nothing controls, with no acceptance                     | one, naming RISK-U-3, that "has a residual level of Medium that needs an acceptance"                                                                                                                                        |
        | block-residual                | the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-3, Critical × Likely, residual probability Likely, accepted                          | "risk RISK-R-3 has an unacceptable residual level of Block"                                                                                                                                                                 |
        | unaccepted-medium             | the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-4 with residual probability Unlikely and no acceptance                               | one, naming RISK-R-4, that "has a residual level of Medium that needs an acceptance"                                                                                                                                        |
        | half-accepted-high            | the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-5 with residual probability Possible, accepted by "QA" with no reason                | one, naming RISK-R-5, that "has a residual level of High that needs an acceptance"                                                                                                                                          |
        | acceptance-not-text           | the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-7 with residual probability Unlikely, accepted by an empty list because "ALARP"      | one, naming RISK-R-7, that "has a residual level of Medium that needs an acceptance"                                                                                                                                        |
        | acceptance-not-words          | the risk policy is declared; RISK-R-8 with residual probability Unlikely, accepted by "QA lead" because true             | one, naming RISK-R-8, that "has a residual level of Medium that needs an acceptance"                                                                                                                                        |
        | bad-status                    | the risk policy is declared; RISK-T-1 of status maybe                                                                    | "risk RISK-T-1 has an unknown status 'maybe' (proposed or approved)"                                                                                                                                                        |
        | proposed                      | the risk policy, of status proposed; RISK-W-1 of status proposed and RISK-W-2 approved; item-01-001 and item-01-002 pass | none, and release passes, warning "risk RISK-W-1 is proposed: a person has not approved its rating" and "the risk policy in documents/risk/policy.md is proposed: a person has not approved it", and nothing about RISK-W-2 |
        | no-status                     | the risk policy, with no status; RISK-W-3 of empty status and RISK-W-4 with none; item-01-001 and item-01-002 pass       | none, and release passes, warning that RISK-W-3, RISK-W-4 and the risk policy are proposed: no status is never approved                                                                                                     |

-- allium: 3
-- .pi/spec/risk/allium/risk.allium
--
-- Scope: the risk context: the risk register kept in the record (the risks of every
-- kind: risk document's frontmatter), each risk scored only against the risk policy the
-- project declares, and the residual decision the release gate holds a release to. The
-- surface is the need this context is home to: risk-register (event-model/area.edn). RDM
-- ships no default policy.

------------------------------------------------------------
-- External Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- The spec RDM reads (specification): a risk's controls are its requirements.
external entity Spec {}

-- One executed test run (test_evidence): a control counts once it has a passing run.
external entity TestRun {}

-- The person who rates the risks and owns the register.
external entity RiskOwnerAccount {}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- The project's risk policy, declared once (risk_policy in a document's frontmatter).
entity RiskPolicy {
    source: String
    severities: List<String>
    probabilities: List<String>
    levels: Map<String, List<String>>           -- one level for each severity and probability pair
    acceptability: Map<String, acceptable | justify | unacceptable>
    status: proposed | approved
}

-- One risk of the register, from the frontmatter of a kind: risk document.
entity Risk {
    id: String
    category: safety | security
    stride: String?                            -- a security risk's STRIDE category
    linked: List<Risk>
    hazard: String
    situation: String
    harm: String
    severity: String
    probability: String
    recorded_level: String?
    controls: List<String>                     -- requirement ids, item-NN-SSS
    residual_severity: String?                 -- defaults to the initial severity
    residual_probability: String?
    accepted_by: String?
    acceptance_rationale: String?
    status: proposed | approved                -- the document's when the risk gives none
    document: String
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Rules
------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Invariants
------------------------------------------------------------

invariant OneRiskPerId {
    for a in Risks:
        for b in Risks:
            a != b implies a.id != b.id
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Actor Declarations
------------------------------------------------------------

actor RiskOwner {
    identified_by: RiskOwnerAccount where true
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Surfaces
------------------------------------------------------------

-- A team can keep its risk register in the record, each risk scored from its own matrix
-- and each control a verified requirement, and cannot release while a risk is unscored,
-- uncontrolled, or residually unacceptable without a named acceptance.
surface RiskRegisterDesk {
    facing owner: RiskOwner
    context risk: Risk

    exposes:
        risk.id
        risk.category
        risk.severity
        risk.probability
        risk.controls
        risk.status

    @guarantee RegisterReadFromFrontmatter
        -- Every field of a risk is read from the frontmatter of a kind: risk document,
        -- and a risk is evaluated only against the one risk policy the project declares.

    @guarantee MalformedRegisterBlocks
        -- A register or policy that cannot be evaluated as written (a missing or
        -- duplicate id, an empty part, an unknown category, an undefined or mis-scored
        -- level, a control that is no requirement, controls with no residual) blocks
        -- release, naming the risk or the document.

    @guarantee UncontrolledRiskBlocks
        -- A residual not evaluated (a control with no passing test), unacceptable, or
        -- acceptable only with a justification nobody recorded blocks release, as does
        -- an unknown status; a proposed rating only warns.

    @guarantee RisksProjectedWithShapes
        -- The register is projected into the graph, each risk with its residual
        -- decision, and the graph's shapes block exactly what the release gate blocks.
}

docs.text: Slice 03-test_evidence of RDM's spec, written the Löyly way in .pi/spec/test_evidence/, read as the release gate reads it. Each user need is a screen of the event model, linked to its Allium surface; each accepted scenario, stamped with an id, is a requirement.

docs.title: User needs
docs.text: This context is home to no user need: its requirements address needs of other contexts.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Requirement Scenario Addresses Rule item-03-001 An unreadable result blocks release and is named, and a failed step fails its run release/trace-verification A result RDM cannot read is never counted as a pass item-03-002 The pytest plugin labels each run of a claiming test with the commit under test release/trace-verification A run that claims a requirement carries the commit it tested item-03-003 executor.json and environment.properties name the executor and the environment release/trace-verification The results of an acceptance run record who ran it and where spec.feature 
Feature: Test evidence
  The accepted scenarios of this context: how executed Allure results are
  read as test runs, and what an acceptance run records about the version it
  tested and who ran it. Each is stamped with an item id that is never
  renumbered or reused, and verified by the acceptance tests whose Allure
  results carry that id as a tag label.

  Rule: A result RDM cannot read is never counted as a pass

    # ../release/allium/release.allium, surface TraceVerification, guarantee UnreadableResultNeverPasses;
    # test-evidence.allium, rule ReadAllureResult (requires 1 to 4)
    @allium-guarantee.UnreadableResultNeverPasses
    @item-03-001
    Scenario: An unreadable result blocks release and is named, and a failed step fails its run
      Given a spec whose only requirement is item-01-001, addressing the need Release
      And a passing Allure result "a" tagged item-01-001
      Then the release gate passes
      When a result "b" is added that cannot be read, holding any of:
        | content                                                         |
        | JSON cut short after '"value": "item-01-001"'                   |
        | a JSON list, not an object                                      |
        | bytes that are not UTF-8                                        |
      Then release is blocked: the result is unreadable, and it could hold a failed run
      When result "b" is a failed run tagged item-01-001 written with a byte-order mark
      Then it is read, and release is blocked: item-01-001 failed
      When a result "b" tagged item-01-001, beside the passing result "a", has any of:
        | case          | what is wrong                                   |
        | capital-status| the status "Failed", which Allure does not write|
        | no-status     | no status                                       |
        | null-status   | a null status                                   |
        | labels-text   | labels given as the text "tag=item-01-001"      |
        | tag-list      | a tag label whose value is a list               |
        | link          | it is a symbolic link to a result elsewhere     |
        | deep          | JSON nested 100000 levels deep                  |
      Then release is blocked by that unreadable result alone
      When failing runs beside the passing result "a" are tagged "Item-01-001", "item_01_001", "item–01-001" and "item-01-777"
      Then release passes, and the gate warns "Allure result tag <tag> matches no requirement" for each of the four
      When a run marked passed has an inner step that failed, and another an inner step that broke
      Then both runs have failed, and so have the requirements they claim
      When a result "x-result.json" cannot be read and verify is run
      Then verify exits non-zero and the verification data lists x-result.json as unreadable

  Rule: A run that claims a requirement carries the commit it tested

    # ../release/allium/release.allium, surface TraceVerification, guarantee RunLabelledWithTheCommitUnderTest;
    # test-evidence.allium, rule LabelRun
    @allium-guarantee.RunLabelledWithTheCommitUnderTest
    @item-03-002
    Scenario: The pytest plugin labels each run of a claiming test with the commit under test
      Given a committed repository whose spec holds item-01-001 and item-01-002, with its DHF in sw/dhf
      And tests test_alarm tagged item-01-001, test_log tagged item-01-002, test_undeclared tagged item-01-099 and test_untagged with no tag
      When the tests run with rdm.pytest_plugin on a clean working tree
      Then the results of test_alarm and test_log carry the commit label of the repository's HEAD
      And test_alarm carries no worktree label
      And test_undeclared and test_untagged carry no commit label
      When the test file has an edit not yet committed and the tests run again
      Then test_alarm carries the worktree label "dirty" and still the commit label of HEAD

  Rule: The results of an acceptance run record who ran it and where

    # ../release/allium/release.allium, surface TraceVerification, guarantee RunRecordsWhoRanItAndWhere;
    # test-evidence.allium, rule RecordRunEnvironment
    @allium-guarantee.RunRecordsWhoRanItAndWhere
    @item-03-003
    Scenario: executor.json and environment.properties name the executor and the environment
      Given a committed repository whose two tests claim item-01-001
      When the tests run with rdm.pytest_plugin on GitHub Actions, run 7001 attempt 2, run number 42 of the workflow "Design controls" in acme/device, by octocat on a pull_request, on a Linux X64 runner
      Then executor.json names "GitHub Actions" of type github, build order 42, the build name "Design controls #42" and the URL https://github.com/acme/device/actions/runs/7001/attempts/2
      And environment.properties records the operating system, the Python, pytest, allure-pytest and RDM versions
      And the commit under test with the worktree "clean"
      And ci.actor octocat, ci.workflow "Design controls", ci.event pull_request and ci.runner "Linux X64", and no user
      When the tests run locally with an uncommitted file in the repository
      Then executor.json names a local run with the build name "<user>@<host>"
      And environment.properties records the user and no ci. entry
      And the commit under test with the worktree "dirty"
      And executor.json and environment.properties sit beside the two tests' results
      When the tests run from a copy of the repository outside git
      Then the commit and the worktree are both recorded as "unknown"

-- .pi/spec/test_evidence/allium/test-evidence.allium
--
-- Scope: the test evidence context: executed Allure results read as test runs, and what
-- an acceptance run records about itself (rdm.pytest_plugin). This context is home to no
-- need and declares no surface: its requirements address release/trace-verification
-- through guarantees declared on release's TraceVerification surface
-- (../../release/allium/release.allium).

------------------------------------------------------------
-- External Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- The spec RDM reads (specification): the ids a run may claim.
external entity Spec {}

-- The repository whose commit a run tested.
external entity Repository {}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- One execution of a test, at one commit, by one executor.
entity TestRun {
    name: String
    test: String
    status: passed | failed | broken | skipped
    claims: List<String>
    commit: String
    worktree: clean | dirty | unknown
    steps: List<Step>
    attachments: List<Attachment>
}

-- A verification step of a run, with its own result; steps nest.
entity Step {
    name: String
    status: passed | failed | broken | skipped
    steps: List<Step>
}

-- What a run kept: a file named in the result.
entity Attachment {
    name: String
    type: String
    source: String
}

-- Who or what ran the tests, and where.
entity Executor {
    name: String
    type: String
    build_name: String
    build_url: String
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Rules
------------------------------------------------------------

-- Read one Allure result file as a test run. What cannot be read is unreadable, never
-- skipped: it could hold a failed run.
rule ReadAllureResult {
    when: ReadAllureResult(file)
    -- 1. the file is UTF-8 JSON (a byte-order mark is allowed), an object, not too deep
    requires: is_json_object(file)
    -- 2. it is a regular file, not a symbolic link
    requires: not is_link(file)
    -- 3. its status is one Allure writes
    requires: file.status in [passed, failed, broken, skipped, unknown]
    -- 4. its labels are name and value text
    requires: for label in file.labels: is_text(label.name) and is_text(label.value)
    ensures:
        TestRun.created(name: file.name, status: worst(file.status, file.steps),
                        claims: tag_labels(file))
        ResultRead(file: file)
}

-- Label a run of a test that claims a requirement of the spec with the commit under test.
rule LabelRun {
    when: LabelRun(run, repository)
    requires: run.claims intersects spec.requirements
    ensures:
        run.commit = repository.head
        run.worktree = if repository.has_uncommitted_changes then dirty else clean
        RunLabelled(run: run)
}

-- Record, once per acceptance run, its executor and its environment.
rule RecordRunEnvironment {
    when: RecordRunEnvironment(results, repository)
    ensures:
        Executor.created(name: ci_or_local(), build_name: build_name(), build_url: build_url())
        RunEnvironmentRecorded(results: results)
}

docs.text:
Requirement Scenario Addresses Rule item-04-001 The release gate passes only when every requirement has a passing run and none fails release/release-blocked A release is blocked until the spec is read whole and every requirement has a passing run item-04-002 Verified, failed and untested come from the runs that carry each requirement's id release/trace-verification Each requirement's status is reconciled from the tag labels of executed Allure results item-04-003 The evidence bundle holds the verification data, the rendered matrix, the report and the results release/release-evidence A release's evidence is retained as one bundle, generated from the record, never mixed with an earlier one item-04-004 The reusable workflow and the gates action run RDM's gates at the revision the caller pins specification/adopt-repository RDM's gates can be reused in another repository's CI, pinned to one RDM revision spec.feature 
Feature: Release
  The accepted scenarios of this context: what holds a release back, how a
  requirement's status is traced from executed results, what a release
  retains, and RDM's gates for other repositories' CI. Each is stamped with
  an item id that is never renumbered or reused, and verified by the
  acceptance tests whose Allure results carry that id as a tag label.

  Rule: A release is blocked until the spec is read whole and every requirement has a passing run

    # release.allium, rule ReleaseGate (requires 1 to 6)
    @allium-rule-success.ReleaseGate @allium-rule-failure.ReleaseGate.1 @allium-rule-failure.ReleaseGate.2
    @allium-rule-failure.ReleaseGate.3 @allium-rule-failure.ReleaseGate.4 @allium-rule-failure.ReleaseGate.5
    @allium-rule-failure.ReleaseGate.6
    @item-04-001
    Scenario: The release gate passes only when every requirement has a passing run and none fails
      Given a spec whose feature file stamps item-01-001 and item-01-002, both addressing the need Release
      When the release manager runs the release gate with no Allure results
      Then release is blocked, item-01-001 and item-01-002 untested
      When a passing run tagged item-01-001 is added
      Then release is blocked, naming item-01-002 and not item-01-001
      When a failing run tagged item-01-002 is added
      Then release is blocked: item-01-002 failed
      When item-01-002's run passes and a failing run tagged item-01-001 is added
      Then release is blocked, naming item-01-001: one passing run does not outweigh a failing one
      When the failing run of item-01-001 is removed
      Then release passes
      When an unstamped scenario "an unstamped behaviour" is added to the feature file
      Then release is blocked, naming "an unstamped behaviour"
      When a second scenario is stamped item-01-001 instead
      Then release is blocked: item-01-001 is stamped twice
      When a feature file "broken.feature" that Gherkin cannot parse is added instead
      Then release is blocked, naming broken.feature
      And a slice of a Löyly plan whose spec.feature is missing (a link to a folder git never received) blocks release, naming the slice
      When the feature file holds no stamped scenario
      Then release is blocked: there is nothing to verify
      And a repository with no spec at all is blocked: no spec was found

  Rule: Each requirement's status is reconciled from the tag labels of executed Allure results

    # release.allium, rule Verify
    @allium-rule-success.Verify
    @item-04-002
    Scenario: Verified, failed and untested come from the runs that carry each requirement's id
      Given Allure results: run p passed tagged item-01-001, run f failed tagged item-01-002, run s skipped tagged item-01-003, run b broken tagged item-01-004
      When the requirements item-01-001 to item-01-005 are reconciled against them
      Then item-01-001 is verified
      And item-01-002 and item-01-004 have failed
      And item-01-003 and item-01-005 are untested
      When a failing run names item-01-001 only as its story, feature and epic labels
      Then item-01-001 is still verified: only a tag label claims a requirement
      When a passing run carries the tag label "@item-01-005"
      Then item-01-005 is verified: the "@" before the id is read
      When item-01-001 to item-01-003 address the need Release, item-01-004 and item-01-005 the need Trace, and verify writes the verification data
      Then the traceability matrix rendered from it shows each requirement's status under the need it addresses

  Rule: A release's evidence is retained as one bundle, generated from the record, never mixed with an earlier one

    # release.allium, rule EvidenceBundle (requires 1 to 2)
    @allium-rule-success.EvidenceBundle @allium-rule-failure.EvidenceBundle.1 @allium-rule-failure.EvidenceBundle.2
    @item-04-003
    Scenario: The evidence bundle holds the verification data, the rendered matrix, the report and the results
      Given a record with a spec, a traceability matrix template and Allure results with attachments and a container
      When the release manager writes the evidence bundle to an output directory apart from the results
      Then the bundle holds the verification data computed from the executed results
      And the traceability matrix rendered from it, with no template markers left
      And the executed results with every attachment and container they reference
      And the verification report, or the manifest says why it is not there
      And a manifest listing exactly the files bundled
      And a symbolic link among the results is not followed, and a missing attachment is listed in the manifest
      And an unreadable result is named in the manifest
      When the bundle is written again over the earlier one
      Then its results replace the earlier bundle's, never mixed with them
      When the output directory would hold the results or sit inside them
      Then the bundle is refused and the results are left untouched
      When the record has no traceability matrix template
      Then the bundle is refused, naming the missing template, and no bundle is written

  Rule: RDM's gates can be reused in another repository's CI, pinned to one RDM revision

    # ../specification/allium/scaffolding.allium, surface AdoptRepository, guarantee GatesReusableInCi
    @allium-guarantee.GatesReusableInCi
    @item-04-004
    Scenario: The reusable workflow and the gates action run RDM's gates at the revision the caller pins
      Given the composite gates action, the reusable gates workflow and the documents action
      When the gates action is run with the checklist part11_document_control over a record with results
      Then it runs verify, the release gate, graph validation and the evidence bundle with the verification report, in that order
      And graph validation holds the documents to the checklists named
      And a gate that fails fails the action
      And with the release gate off and no results yet, no gate runs
      And every rdm command the workflow and the actions run is one RDM's command line accepts
      And the action installs RDM from its own revision, the workflow from the revision the caller pins, never from a package index
      And the reusable workflow runs the caller's acceptance tests before the gates
      And the documents action renders with the image of the release it is pinned to, else the latest image
      And the workflow rdm adopt lays down calls the reusable workflow pinned to the installed RDM's version
      And RDM's own CI calls the same workflow, pinned to the commit under test

-- allium: 3
-- .pi/spec/release/allium/release.allium
--
-- Scope: the release context: whether a commit may be released (the release gate), each
-- requirement's verification status from executed Allure results (verify), and the
-- retained evidence of a release (the evidence bundle). The surfaces are the needs this
-- context is home to: release-blocked, trace-verification, release-evidence
-- (event-model/area.edn).

------------------------------------------------------------
-- External Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- The spec RDM reads (specification): its requirements and the needs they address.
external entity Spec {}

-- One executed test run, read from an Allure result (test_evidence).
external entity TestRun {}

-- The person who releases a version of the product.
external entity ReleaseManagerAccount {}

-- The person who keeps the record.
external entity AuthorAccount {}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- A requirement's verification status, reconciled from the runs that carry its id.
entity Verification {
    requirement: String
    status: verified | failed | untested
    runs: List<TestRun>
}

-- The retained evidence of one release, written apart from the results it bundles.
entity EvidenceBundle {
    output: String
    files: List<String>
    manifest: String
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Rules
------------------------------------------------------------

-- Reconcile every requirement of the spec against the tag labels of the executed results.
-- A run claims a requirement only by an Allure tag label of its id (a leading "@" is
-- dropped). Passed verifies; failed or broken fails; skipped, or no run, leaves untested.
rule Verify {
    when: Verify(author, dhf, results)
    ensures:
        for requirement in spec.requirements:
            Verification.created(requirement: requirement, status: status_of(requirement, results))
        VerificationRecorded(dhf: dhf)
}

-- Decide whether the commit may be released.
rule ReleaseGate {
    when: ReleaseGate(manager, dhf, results)
    -- 1. a spec is found
    requires: exists spec
    -- 2. it is read whole: no file Gherkin cannot parse
    requires: spec.problems = []
    -- 3. no scenario without an item id
    requires: spec.unstamped = []
    -- 4. no item id on two scenarios
    requires: spec.duplicates = []
    -- 5. at least one requirement
    requires: spec.requirements != []
    -- 6. every requirement verified: a passing run and no failing one
    requires: for requirement in spec.requirements: status_of(requirement, results) = verified
    -- 7. every Allure result read: one RDM cannot read could hold a failed run
    requires: unreadable(results) = []
    -- 8. every user need addressed by a requirement
    requires: for need in spec.needs: addressed(need)
    -- 9. every risk evaluated, its residual acceptable or accepted (risk/risk.allium)
    requires: risk_findings(dhf, results) = []
    ensures: ReleaseGatePassed(dhf: dhf)
}

-- Write the retained evidence of a release.
rule EvidenceBundle {
    when: EvidenceBundle(manager, dhf, results, output)
    -- 1. the output neither holds the results nor sits inside them
    requires: not overlaps(output, results)
    -- 2. the record has a traceability matrix template to render
    requires: exists dhf.traceability_matrix_template
    ensures:
        EvidenceBundle.created(output: output)
        EvidenceBundleWritten(output: output)
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Actor Declarations
------------------------------------------------------------

actor ReleaseManager {
    identified_by: ReleaseManagerAccount where true
}

actor RegulatoryAuthor {
    identified_by: AuthorAccount where true
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Surfaces
------------------------------------------------------------

-- A release is blocked until every requirement of the spec is verified by a passing test.
surface ReleaseGateDesk {
    facing manager: ReleaseManager
    context spec: Spec

    provides:
        ReleaseGate(manager, dhf, results)
}

-- Each requirement's verification status is traceable from executed test results.
surface TraceVerification {
    facing author: RegulatoryAuthor
    context spec: Spec

    provides:
        Verify(author, dhf, results)

    @guarantee SpecNeedsReadFromTheirSource
        -- The user needs come from the source the spec's configuration names (each
        -- Feature by default, or an adapter's richer model) and each requirement
        -- addresses the needs that source links it to.

    @guarantee UnreadableResultNeverPasses
        -- A result RDM cannot read is never counted as a pass: it blocks release and
        -- is named; a run whose step failed or broke has failed.

    @guarantee RunLabelledWithTheCommitUnderTest
        -- A run that claims a requirement carries the commit it tested, and a mark
        -- when the working tree had uncommitted changes.

    @guarantee RunRecordsWhoRanItAndWhere
        -- The results of an acceptance run record its executor and its environment.
}

-- A release's evidence (verification data, traceability matrix, verification report)
-- and the device-master-record index can be produced as retained, generated artifacts
-- from the record.
surface ReleaseEvidence {
    facing manager: ReleaseManager
    context spec: Spec

    provides:
        EvidenceBundle(manager, dhf, results, output)

    @guarantee DmrIndexFromFrontmatter
        -- The device-master-record index lists every controlled document from its own
        -- frontmatter.

    @guarantee VerificationReportForAReviewer
        -- The verification report shows someone who did not run the tests what was
        -- tested, where, by whom, and whether the evidence is release-grade.
}

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Requirement Scenario Addresses Rule item-05-001 Gap analysis names each missing reference and exits non-zero when one is missing or nothing was checked compliance/gap-analysis A document set has a gap for every checklist key no document references item-05-002 The built-in checklists are listed by name, hold unique keys and resolve their includes compliance/gap-analysis RDM ships composable checklists for the applicable standards item-05-003 The coverage report gives each checklist's total, missing, covered and percent compliance/gap-analysis Coverage of a document set is tabulated per checklist item-05-004 RDM's own document-control statement passes the built-in Part 11 checklist, and fails without a control compliance/gap-analysis RDM keeps its own record under the 21 CFR Part 11 checklist it ships spec.feature 
Feature: Compliance
  The accepted scenarios of this context: gap analysis of documents against
  the checklists of the applicable standards, and the checklists RDM ships.
  Each is stamped with an item id that is never renumbered or reused, and
  verified by the acceptance tests whose Allure results carry that id as a tag
  label.

  Rule: A document set has a gap for every checklist key no document references

    # compliance.allium, rule Gap (requires 1 to 3)
    @allium-rule-success.Gap @allium-rule-failure.Gap.1 @allium-rule-failure.Gap.2 @allium-rule-failure.Gap.3
    @item-05-001
    Scenario: Gap analysis names each missing reference and exits non-zero when one is missing or nothing was checked
      Given a checklist "cl.txt" with the clauses X-1 and X-2
      When the regulatory author runs rdm gap cl.txt over "partial.md", which references [[X-1]] only
      Then it exits 3, listing X-2 and not X-1, under the heading "# 1 gap:"
      And over "full.md", which references [[X-1]] and [[X-2]], it exits 0
      And a stray "[[" does not turn the next paragraphs' mentions into references: X-2 is still missing
      And a bare mention "We do not address X-2" is no reference to X-2: it exits 3
      And [[X-12]] does not reference the key X-1: it exits 3
      And [[FDA-SW:sdmp: This document is a pointer document.]] references the key FDA-SW:sdmp: it exits 0
      And [[FDA-SW:sdmp]] does not reference the key FDA-SW: it exits 3
      And a byte-order mark is not part of the first key: a checklist beginning with a byte-order mark before "X-1 first" is covered by full.md
      And "include   cl.txt  " with spaces around the name is resolved
      When nothing could be checked: a checklist with no clauses, a checklist that does not exist, a bare "include", an include of a file that does not exist, a document that does not exist, or a directory given as a document
      Then it exits 2, never 0
      When a document covering every clause still holds a "TODO: write this section" placeholder
      Then it exits 0 and warns, naming the document and its placeholder
      When its report of 20000 gaps is piped into a reader that stops after one line
      Then it ends quietly, with no traceback and no BrokenPipe error

  Rule: RDM ships composable checklists for the applicable standards

    # compliance.allium, surface GapAnalysis, guarantee BuiltInChecklistsCompose
    @allium-guarantee.BuiltInChecklistsCompose
    @item-05-002
    Scenario: The built-in checklists are listed by name, hold unique keys and resolve their includes
      When the regulatory author lists the built-in checklists
      Then 62304_2015_class_b, 14971_2019, FDA-SW_2021_enhanced and csv_tool_validation (computer software validation of a tool) are listed by name
      And IEC 62304, ISO 14971, FDA-SW, FDA-CYBER and FDA-HFE each have a built-in checklist with clauses
      And no built-in checklist holds a key twice
      And 62304_2015_class_b, which includes 62304_2015_class_a by name, requires every clause of class A and more
      Given a checklist "main.txt" with "include base.txt" and the clause M-1, and "base.txt" with the clause B-1
      When a document referencing only [[M-1]] is checked against main.txt
      Then it exits 3: B-1, defined only in the included file, is still required
      And a document referencing [[M-1]] and [[B-1]] exits 0
      Given "a.txt" includes "sub/b.txt", which includes "../a.txt" and "./../a.txt"
      When the coverage of a document referencing [[A-1]] is reported against a.txt
      Then a.txt is read once: its row is "| A.TXT | 2 | 1 | 1 | 50% |" and it exits 3

  Rule: Coverage of a document set is tabulated per checklist

    # compliance.allium, rule Coverage (requires 1)
    @allium-rule-success.Coverage @allium-rule-failure.Coverage.1
    @item-05-003
    Scenario: The coverage report gives each checklist's total, missing, covered and percent
      Given a checklist "iso_checklist.txt" with the clauses ISO-1, ISO-2 and ISO-3
      When the regulatory author reports coverage of "process.md", which references [[ISO-1]] and [[ISO-3]]
      Then the row "| ISO | 3 | 1 | 2 | 66% |" is printed and it exits 3
      And in verbose mode the missing ISO-2 is named
      When the coverage of a document referencing all three clauses is reported
      Then it exits 0, and in verbose mode prints no empty "Missing Items" heading
      When the checklist has no clauses or does not exist
      Then it exits 2: nothing could be checked

  Rule: RDM keeps its own record under the 21 CFR Part 11 checklist it ships

    # compliance.allium, surface GapAnalysis, guarantee Part11ChecklistShipped
    @allium-guarantee.Part11ChecklistShipped
    @item-05-004
    Scenario: RDM's own document-control statement passes the built-in Part 11 checklist, and fails without a control
      When the regulatory author lists the built-in checklists
      Then part11_document_control is listed by name
      When dhf/documents/document_control.md is checked against part11_document_control
      Then it exits 0: the statement references every clause
      When a copy of the statement without its reference [[P11:11.10e]] is checked
      Then it exits 3: dropping one control fails the audit

-- allium: 3
-- .pi/spec/compliance/allium/compliance.allium
--
-- Scope: the compliance context: gap analysis of a document set against the checklist of a
-- standard, the coverage report, and the checklists RDM ships. A reference is a delimited
-- [[KEY]] (or [[KEY: annotation]]); a bare mention, or a longer key, never covers a key.
-- The surface is the need this context is home to: gap-analysis (event-model/area.edn).

------------------------------------------------------------
-- External Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- A document of the record, Markdown, holding [[KEY]] references.
external entity Document {}

-- The person who keeps the record.
external entity AuthorAccount {}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- A checklist: clauses under unique keys, with `include` of other checklists (by built-in
-- name or by path), resolved once each.
entity Checklist {
    name: String
    clauses: List<Clause>
    includes: List<Checklist>
}

entity Clause {
    key: String
    description: String
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Rules
------------------------------------------------------------

-- Report the checklist's keys that no document references (rdm gap). Exits 3 on a gap, 0
-- when every clause is referenced; warns of a document that still holds a placeholder.
rule Gap {
    when: Gap(author, checklist, documents)
    -- 1. the checklist, and every checklist it includes, can be read
    requires: readable(checklist)
    -- 2. the checklist holds at least one clause
    requires: checklist.clauses != []
    -- 3. every document can be read
    requires: for d in documents: readable(d)
    ensures: GapsReported(checklist: checklist, missing: missing(checklist, documents))
}

-- Tabulate, per checklist, total, missing, covered and percent (rdm gap --coverage); in
-- verbose mode, name the missing keys. Exits as Gap does.
rule Coverage {
    when: Coverage(author, checklists, documents)
    -- 1. each checklist can be read and holds at least one clause
    requires: for c in checklists: readable(c) and c.clauses != []
    ensures: CoverageReported(checklists: checklists)
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Actor Declarations
------------------------------------------------------------

actor RegulatoryAuthor {
    identified_by: AuthorAccount where true
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Surfaces
------------------------------------------------------------

-- A regulatory author can check that documents contain the references a chosen standard's
-- checklist requires (gap analysis).
surface GapAnalysis {
    facing author: RegulatoryAuthor
    context checklist: Checklist

    provides:
        Gap(author, checklist, documents)
        Coverage(author, checklists, documents)

    @guarantee BuiltInChecklistsCompose
        -- The standards' checklists ship built in, each with unique keys, and an include
        -- of another checklist by built-in name or path requires its clauses too.

    @guarantee Part11ChecklistShipped
        -- A 21 CFR Part 11 document-control checklist ships built in, and RDM's own
        -- document-control statement passes gap analysis against it.
}
