Feature: Graph
  The accepted scenarios of this context: the record projected into an RDF
  graph that people query and explore and agents read, never edit. Each is
  stamped with an item id that is never renumbered or reused, and verified by
  the acceptance tests whose Allure results carry that id as a tag label.

  Rule: The record is projected into one named graph per source, deterministically

    # graph.allium, surface ExploreGraph, guarantee RecordProjectedPerSource
    @allium-guarantee.RecordProjectedPerSource
    @item-06-001
    Scenario: A committed record becomes a dataset of named graphs, byte-identical while the record is unchanged
      Given a committed repository whose spec holds the needs Alarm and Logging as Features and the requirements item-01-001 and item-01-002 under them
      And controlled documents with id, title and revision, and Allure results
      When the author builds the graph
      Then the record graph holds each user need with its Feature's title as id and its description as text
      And each requirement with its text, the needs it addresses, its context and its source line, and each bounded context
      And read through an adapter (Löyly's layout, Allium), the graph holds what a need faces, provides and guarantees, the rules a requirement covers, the Allium rules, and a context with no requirement
      And each controlled document with its id, title and revision
      And an executions graph only when results are given
      And a git graph with the design document's latest commit, its time and its author
      And an rdfs:label on every typed node
      And an ontology graph of RDM's vocabulary, reusing OSLC RM
      And the dataset is written as sorted N-Quads, byte-identical for an unchanged record
      And a literal holding a Unicode line separator stays one statement

  Rule: The projection is stored, queried and served read-only

    # graph.allium, surface ExploreGraph, guarantee StoreQueriedAndServedReadOnly
    @allium-guarantee.StoreQueriedAndServedReadOnly
    @item-06-002
    Scenario: The store is replaced on each build, queried with SPARQL and served read-only
      Given a graph built into a store from a record with item-01-001 and item-01-002
      When the author queries the store with the standard prefixes undeclared and no GRAPH clause
      Then the query answers over the union of the named graphs
      When item-01-002 is removed and the graph is built again
      Then the store holds no item-01-002: it was replaced, not merged
      And with no store given, the query answers from an in-memory projection, ASK and CONSTRUCT included
      And a SPARQL Update or a SERVICE call is refused: nothing changes, nothing reaches the network
      And FROM, which the union default graph would ignore, is refused, and so is SERVICE with a variable endpoint, while a prefix named service is no call
      When the store is served over HTTP
      Then the endpoint's default graph is the union, the standard prefixes are predeclared and CORS is open
      And an update from another origin is refused and the data stays
      And SERVICE is refused, even after a comment ended by a carriage return
      And the endpoint answers from the last build
      And a store that does not exist is refused, not created

  Rule: Checklists join the graph as data

    # graph.allium, surface ExploreGraph, guarantee ChecklistsAsSkos
    @allium-guarantee.ChecklistsAsSkos
    @item-06-003
    Scenario: A text checklist, a built-in one and an RDF one become SKOS collections of clauses
      Given a text checklist that includes a built-in checklist by name, and a checklist written in RDF
      When the author builds the graph with those checklists
      Then each checklist is a SKOS collection of its own clauses that links the checklists it includes
      And the built-in checklist is resolved by its name
      And each clause has its key, description, standard, edition and nearest listed parent clause
      And the RDF checklist is loaded as it is, its nodes labelled like any other

    # graph.allium, surface ExploreGraph, guarantee DocumentsLinkTheirClauses
    @allium-guarantee.DocumentsLinkTheirClauses
    @item-06-009
    Scenario: A document's reference tags link it to the clauses rdm gap would match
      Given documents whose [[...]] tags reference some clauses of a checklist and not others
      When the author builds the graph with that checklist
      Then each document links to the clauses its tags reference, matched as rdm gap matches keys
      And the clauses no document references are exactly those rdm gap reports missing

  Rule: The gate rules hold over the graph as SHACL shapes

    # graph.allium, surface ExploreGraph, guarantee GateRulesAsShapes
    @allium-guarantee.GateRulesAsShapes
    @item-06-004
    Scenario: The shapes block exactly what the release gate blocks, each finding on its node
      Given records with the requirements item-01-001 and item-01-002, each with these needs and runs:
        | case             | needs               | runs                                              | blocked     |
        | all pass         | Need1, Need2        | item-01-001 passed; item-01-002 passed            | nothing     |
        | failed           | Need1, Need2        | item-01-001 passed and failed; item-01-002 passed | item-01-001 |
        | broken           | Need1, Need2        | item-01-001 passed and broken; item-01-002 passed | item-01-001 |
        | untested         | Need1, Need2        | item-01-001 passed                                | item-01-002 |
        | skipped only     | Need1, Need2        | item-01-001 passed; item-01-002 skipped           | item-01-002 |
        | unaddressed need | Need1, Need2, Need3 | item-01-001 passed; item-01-002 passed            | Need3       |
      When the shapes are validated over each record's graph and the release gate is run on it
      Then for each case both block exactly what the table names
      When the needs are Need1, Need2 and Need3 and item-01-001's only run failed
      Then Need3 is a violation "user need is addressed by no requirement"
      And item-01-001 is a violation "requirement has a failed or broken test run"
      And item-01-002 is a violation "requirement is not verified by any passing test run"
      And a checklist clause no document references, and a clause without a key or a standard, are violations
      And a requirement addressing no user need, and a run claiming an id that is no requirement, are warnings
      And what the release gate blocks about the whole record, the shapes block too
      And the executions graph reads results as the gates do: a byte-order mark is read, a failed step fails its run

    # graph.allium, rule GraphValidate (requires 1 to 2)
    @allium-rule-success.GraphValidate @allium-rule-failure.GraphValidate.1 @allium-rule-failure.GraphValidate.2
    @item-06-010
    Scenario: rdm graph validate reports each result and exits on a violation
      Given a record whose graph has violations, and one without
      When the author runs rdm graph validate on each
      Then each result is a line with its severity, focus node and message
      And the command exits 1 on the record with violations and 0 on the other
      And a user-supplied shapes file adds its rules as data
      When a shapes or checklist file is not RDF
      Then the command reports an error and exits 2, never with a traceback

  Rule: The graph can be opened in AWS Graph Explorer as a file

    # graph.allium, rule ExplorerFile (requires 1)
    @allium-rule-success.ExplorerFile @allium-rule-failure.ExplorerFile.1
    @item-06-005
    Scenario: The whole record is written as a Graph Explorer file, a class left out on request
      Given a record with needs, requirements, documents, risks and test runs
      When the author writes the graph as a Graph Explorer file
      Then the file has Graph Explorer's envelope and connection
      And every node of the record, of every kind, and nothing from the vocabulary
      And every link between two record nodes, in Graph Explorer's edge-id form, and no rdf:type statement
      When a class is left out
      Then its nodes and their links are dropped, with the nodes that hang only from them, and only those
      And the command writes the file from a fresh projection or from a built store
      When a class to leave out is one the graph does not have
      Then it is refused, naming the classes the graph has

  Rule: An agent reads the record through four read-only tools

    # graph.allium, rule ServeAgent
    @allium-rule-success.ServeAgent
    @item-06-006
    Scenario: The agent server answers schema, query, trace and validate from the current record
      Given a record with the needs Alarm and Logging, the requirements item-01-001 and item-01-002, and a passing run of item-01-001
      When an agent connects to rdm graph mcp
      Then it is offered exactly four tools: schema, query, trace and validate
      And schema gives the vocabulary and the predeclared prefixes
      And query answers SPARQL with those prefixes predeclared
      And trace of item-01-001 gives its scenario, context, source, needs, coverage and runs
      And trace of a need gives its text, context and requirements, and what an adapter adds (faces, provides, guarantees) is empty
      And validate gives the gate shapes' results: item-01-002 has no passing run
      When the record is edited during the session
      Then the next call answers from the edited record

    # graph.allium, surface AgentReadsRecord, guarantee AgentCannotChangeTheRecord
    @allium-guarantee.AgentCannotChangeTheRecord
    @item-06-007
    Scenario: The agent server cannot change the record or reach the network
      Given the agent server over a record
      Then its four tools are all declared read-only and non-destructive
      When the agent sends every form of SPARQL Update
      Then each is refused and nothing in the record changed
      When the agent sends SERVICE in any case, with an IRI or a variable endpoint
      Then it is refused, while the word inside a literal is just text
      When the agent traces input that is not id-shaped
      Then it is refused as "not an id"
      And trace answers an id the record declares whatever its shape, such as the need Logging, and nothing built from it
      And SELECT, ASK, CONSTRUCT and DESCRIBE all work
      And rows beyond the cap are cut and the cut is reported; under the cap nothing is flagged

  Rule: Risks are in the graph, with shapes that block what the release gate blocks

    # ../risk/allium/risk.allium, surface RiskRegisterDesk, guarantee RisksProjectedWithShapes
    @allium-guarantee.RisksProjectedWithShapes
    @item-06-008
    Scenario: Each risk's facts are in the risks graph, and the shapes block the risks the gate blocks
      Given a risk register with safety and security risks, their scores, controls and acceptances, and a risk policy
      When the graph is built
      Then the risks graph holds each risk's facts: category, STRIDE category, linked risks, hazard, situation, harm, scores, levels, residual decision, status, controls and acceptance
      And the residual decision is "not evaluated" until every control has a passing test
      And trace gives a risk with each controlling requirement, and a requirement with the risks it controls
      And the shapes block exactly the risks the release gate blocks, case by case
      When the risk policy is malformed
      Then the gate blocks, and the shapes block every risk with its message
      When a risk has no id
      Then the gate blocks it, and so do the shapes, on a stand-in node
      When a finding about the register has no risk to carry it
      Then the gate blocks, and so do the shapes, on a stand-in node for the register

    # graph.allium, surface ExploreGraph, guarantee RiskLinkedToItsPolicy
    @allium-guarantee.RiskLinkedToItsPolicy
    @item-06-012
    Scenario: A risk links to the document of the policy it was evaluated against
      Given a risk register and a document declaring the risk policy
      When the graph is built
      Then each risk links to the policy's document
      And without a policy, a risk links to none

  Rule: Each controlled document carries who landed its latest change

    # graph.allium, surface ExploreGraph, guarantee LandingCommitRecorded
    @allium-guarantee.LandingCommitRecorded
    @item-06-011
    Scenario: A document's latest change is recorded with the commit that landed it on the default branch
      Given a change to SDS-1 on a feature branch, which goes on after the change while main moves on
      When someone else merges the branch into main, and later work lands on main
      Then SDS-1's latest change is authored on the branch and landed by the merge, with the merge's author
      And the landing is still the merge, not the newest commit
      When a change is on a branch that has not landed
      Then the document has no landing facts and a warning names it
      When the latest change is a direct commit on main
      Then it landed in itself, by its own author, and nothing warns
      And every controlled document has its commit and landing, the V&V plan as well as the design documents
      And in a repository with no remote whose one branch is neither main nor master, that branch is the default

  Rule: A run carries what it recorded, and nothing the record already holds

    # graph.allium, surface ExploreGraph, guarantee StepsAndAttachmentsCarried
    @allium-guarantee.StepsAndAttachmentsCarried
    @item-06-013
    Scenario: A run's steps and attachments are in the graph and in trace
      Given an Allure result with nested steps and attachments on the run and on a step
      When the graph is built
      Then the run carries its steps in order and nested, each with its name and status
      And its attachments, on the run and on the step, each with its name, media type and file
      And trace lists them with the run, nested and ordered

    # graph.allium, surface ExploreGraph, guarantee OnlyDesignControlFactsProjected
    @allium-guarantee.OnlyDesignControlFactsProjected
    @item-06-014
    Scenario: A result is projected in full, but not what claims nothing about design controls
      Given a failed Allure result with a uuid, a full name, start and stop times, a status message and trace, parameters, labels and links, and a container with fixtures
      When the graph is built
      Then the run carries its uuid, name and times, its status message and trace, and its parameters as name and value
      And its labels are not nodes, its links, a test case per history id and the container fixtures are not projected
      And its item tag and output labels still link the run to its requirement and its code

  Rule: Bounded contexts and documents link to each other from the record

    # graph.allium, surface ExploreGraph, guarantee ContextsLinkedToTheirDocuments
    @allium-guarantee.ContextsLinkedToTheirDocuments
    @item-06-015
    Scenario: Contexts link to the documents that declare them, and documents to the ones they reference
      Given design documents whose frontmatter declares contexts with their part and references other documents
      When the graph is built
      Then each bounded context links to the document whose contexts frontmatter declares it, with its part
      And each controlled document links to the controlled documents its references frontmatter names
      And the traceability matrix template, an output, is not projected
      And once any document declares contexts, a shape warns on a context no document declares
      And validation fails on a reference to a document the record does not hold
      And a context may be declared by id alone, and a single reference may be a string

  Rule: Evidence is tied to the version of the product it tested

    # graph.allium, surface ExploreGraph, guarantee EvidenceTiedToTheProductCommit
    @allium-guarantee.EvidenceTiedToTheProductCommit
    @item-06-016
    Scenario: Each run links to the commit it tested, and a run of another commit than the product's is stale
      Given a record at commit HEAD, and runs labelled with HEAD (one clean, one dirty), with an older commit, and with none
      When the graph is built and validated
      Then each run links to the commit its commit label names
      And the record carries the commit it was built at and the product's commit, its own
      And the run of uncommitted changes is marked and the clean one is not
      And a shape warns on the run tied to no commit
      And a shape warns on the run of the older commit: another commit than the product's
      When the spec lives in a repository of its own
      Then the product's commit is that repository's, the record's stays its own
      And a run of the product's commit is current, and a run of the record's commit is stale
allium/graph.allium 
-- allium: 3
-- .pi/spec/graph/allium/graph.allium
--
-- Scope: the graph context: the record projected into an RDF dataset (one named graph
-- per source), stored, queried and served read-only, checked by SHACL shapes that
-- express the gate rules, written as an AWS Graph Explorer file, and read by agents
-- through a read-only MCP server. The graph is never edited: it is rebuilt from the
-- record. The surfaces are the needs this context is home to: explore-graph and
-- agent-reads-record (event-model/area.edn).

------------------------------------------------------------
-- External Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- The record: the spec, the controlled documents, the risk register, git history.
external entity Record {}

-- Executed Allure results, when given.
external entity Results {}

-- A regulatory checklist, in rdm gap's text format or RDF.
external entity Checklist {}

-- The person who keeps and explores the record.
external entity AuthorAccount {}

-- An agent, in any harness, reading the record.
external entity AgentSession {}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- The projected dataset, in a store each build replaces.
entity GraphStore {
    location: String
    named_graphs: List<String>
}

-- A result of the gate shapes: its severity, focus node and message.
entity ShapeResult {
    severity: Violation | Warning
    focus: String
    message: String
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Rules
------------------------------------------------------------

-- Project the record into its named graphs and replace the store with them.
rule GraphBuild {
    when: GraphBuild(author, dhf, results, checklists)
    ensures:
        GraphStore.replaced(named_graphs: project(dhf, results, checklists))
        GraphBuilt(dhf: dhf)
}

-- Validate the gate shapes, and any shapes the author supplies, over the projection.
rule GraphValidate {
    when: GraphValidate(author, dhf, results, checklists, shapes)
    -- 1. every shapes file is RDF
    requires: for file in shapes: is_rdf(file)
    -- 2. every checklist file is a checklist rdm gap reads, or RDF
    requires: for file in checklists: is_checklist(file)
    ensures:
        for result in shacl(project(dhf, results, checklists), shapes):
            ShapeResult.created(severity: result.severity, focus: result.focus, message: result.message)
        GraphValidated(dhf: dhf, violations: count(Violation))
}

-- Write the graph as an AWS Graph Explorer file, leaving out the classes asked.
rule ExplorerFile {
    when: ExplorerFile(author, dhf, results, leave_out)
    -- 1. every class to leave out is a class the graph has
    requires: for class in leave_out: class in classes(project(dhf, results))
    ensures: ExplorerFileWritten(dhf: dhf)
}

-- Serve the record to an agent over stdio: schema, query, trace and validate, each
-- answering from a projection rebuilt on that call.
rule ServeAgent {
    when: ServeAgent(agent, dhf, results)
    ensures: AgentServed(dhf: dhf)
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Actor Declarations
------------------------------------------------------------

actor RegulatoryAuthor {
    identified_by: AuthorAccount where true
}

actor Agent {
    identified_by: AgentSession where true
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Surfaces
------------------------------------------------------------

-- A regulatory author can query and visually explore the record as a linked graph,
-- without changing how the record is written.
surface ExploreGraph {
    facing author: RegulatoryAuthor
    context record: Record

    provides:
        GraphBuild(author, dhf, results, checklists)
        GraphValidate(author, dhf, results, checklists, shapes)
        ExplorerFile(author, dhf, results, leave_out)

    @guarantee RecordProjectedPerSource
        -- One named graph per source (record, executions, git, ontology), every typed
        -- node labelled, written as sorted N-Quads, byte-identical for an unchanged record.

    @guarantee StoreQueriedAndServedReadOnly
        -- Each build replaces the store; queries and the HTTP endpoint read it, over the
        -- union of the named graphs, and refuse updates and SERVICE calls.

    @guarantee ChecklistsAsSkos
        -- A checklist joins the graph as a SKOS collection of its clauses, linking the
        -- checklists it includes.

    @guarantee GateRulesAsShapes
        -- SHACL shapes block exactly what the release gate blocks, each result on its node.

    @guarantee DocumentsLinkTheirClauses
        -- A document links to the clauses its reference tags name, matched as rdm gap
        -- matches, so an unreferenced clause is one rdm gap reports missing.

    @guarantee LandingCommitRecorded
        -- Each controlled document carries the commit that landed its latest change on the
        -- default branch, with that commit's author.

    @guarantee RiskLinkedToItsPolicy
        -- Each risk links to the document holding the policy it was evaluated against.

    @guarantee StepsAndAttachmentsCarried
        -- A run carries its steps, nested and ordered, and its attachments.

    @guarantee OnlyDesignControlFactsProjected
        -- A result is projected in full, but not what the record already holds or what
        -- claims nothing about design controls.

    @guarantee ContextsLinkedToTheirDocuments
        -- Each bounded context links to the document declaring it; each document to the
        -- documents it references.

    @guarantee EvidenceTiedToTheProductCommit
        -- Each run links to the commit it tested; a run of another commit than the
        -- product's is stale evidence.
}

-- An agent, in any harness, can read the record (query it, trace a requirement or need to
-- its tests and results, check it against the gate rules) and cannot change it.
surface AgentReadsRecord {
    facing agent: Agent
    context record: Record

    provides:
        ServeAgent(agent, dhf, results)

    @guarantee AgentCannotChangeTheRecord
        -- Four read-only tools: no SPARQL Update, no SERVICE call, trace only of ids, and
        -- results capped with the cut reported.
}

Requirement Scenario Addresses Rule item-07-001 rdm render fills a Markdown template from data files, each under its file name publishing/compile-dhf A document is a Markdown template rendered against the data files supplied, never against a value they lack item-07-002 invert_dependencies, join_to, md_indent, glob, include and gherkin build traceability tables and final documents publishing/compile-dhf Templates have the filters a traceability table needs item-07-003 Sections are numbered, a second render gets the first's words, and auditor-only notes are removed publishing/compile-dhf Rendered Markdown is post-processed: numbered, given its own words, and stripped of auditor-only notes item-07-004 The lines between RDOC and ENDRDOC are a snippet under its key publishing/compile-dhf Code snippets are extracted from source files for inclusion in documents item-07-005 IFU-001 lists the manual's pages in the reading order of instructions for use, behind a cover publishing/user-manual RDM's user manual is one controlled document, published per release, that discloses every risk item-07-006 The manual is published once per release tag and once for the development version publishing/user-manual RDM's user manual is one controlled document, published per release, that discloses every risk item-07-007 The manual's "Limits and risks" chapter discloses every risk of the register by its id publishing/user-manual RDM's user manual is one controlled document, published per release, that discloses every risk item-07-008 The DMR index has one entry per controlled document, from its frontmatter release/release-evidence The device-master-record index and the verification report are generated from the record item-07-009 The verification report shows a reviewer who did not run the tests what was verified release/release-evidence The device-master-record index and the verification report are generated from the record spec.feature 
Feature: Publishing
  The accepted scenarios of this context: compiling the design history file
  from the record (templates and data to Markdown, its filters, its
  post-processing, snippets from source), RDM's own user manual, and the
  generated release documents (the device-master-record index and the
  verification report). Each is stamped with an item id that is never
  renumbered or reused, and verified by the acceptance tests whose Allure
  results carry that id as a tag label.

  Rule: A document is a Markdown template rendered against the data files supplied, never against a value they lack

    # publishing.allium, rule Render (requires 1 to 2)
    @allium-rule-success.Render @allium-rule-failure.Render.1 @allium-rule-failure.Render.2
    @item-07-001
    Scenario: rdm render fills a Markdown template from data files, each under its file name
      Given a template doc.md "# {{ device.name }}" then "Version {{ device.version }}, by {{ other.maker }}."
      And the data files empty.yml, device.yml with name "Acme Monitor" and version "1.2", and other.yml with maker "Acme Inc"
      When the regulatory author runs rdm render doc.md with empty.yml, device.yml and other.yml
      Then the output is "# Acme Monitor", then "Version 1.2, by Acme Inc."
      When other.yml is left out
      Then rendering is refused with exit status 2, naming "other" and doc.md
      When the template nope.md does not exist
      Then rendering is refused with exit status 2, naming nope.md

  Rule: Templates have the filters a traceability table needs

    # publishing.allium, surface CompileDhf, guarantee TraceabilityFilters
    @allium-guarantee.TraceabilityFilters
    @item-07-002
    Scenario: invert_dependencies, join_to, md_indent, glob, include and gherkin build traceability tables and final documents
      Given items with id A depending on B
      When a template inverts them with invert_dependencies('id', 'deps')
      Then B is depended on by ['A']
      Given a table with rows r1 (v 1) and r2 (v 2)
      When a template joins ['r2', 'r1'] to it with join_to
      Then it reads the rows in that order: "2;1;"
      When a template indents the snippet "# Title" with md_indent(header_shift=1)
      Then it reads "## Title"
      Given feature files spec/b/spec.feature ("Feature: B") and spec/a/spec.feature, and a document arch.md with frontmatter id SDS-1 and the heading "# Architecture"
      When a template includes every file 'spec/*/spec.feature' | glob gives, and 'arch.md' | include | md_indent(1)
      Then it carries spec/a/spec.feature, then spec/b/spec.feature, each as written, and "## Architecture" without the frontmatter
      Given a feature file with a Rule "Within 2 s", a scenario tagged @smoke @allium-rule-success.Raise @REQ-12 whose steps hold "$140" and "<value>", an outline @REQ-13 with Examples, and a comment
      When a template lays it out with gherkin, given verification data in which REQ-12 is verified by 2 runs
      Then it is Markdown marked for the templates: the Rule a rule-line, each scenario a scenario-card led by its id and, for REQ-12, "✓ verified · 2 runs", its steps' keywords marked, the outline's Examples a table, what its tags cover in words ("rule Raise (success)", "need Alarm"), "$" and "<" escaped, and the comment left out
      When rdm render joins the id r9 to a table holding only r1
      Then rendering exits with status 2, naming r9

  Rule: Rendered Markdown is post-processed: numbered, given its own words, and stripped of auditor-only notes

    # publishing.allium, surface CompileDhf, guarantee MarkdownPostProcessed
    @allium-guarantee.MarkdownPostProcessed
    @item-07-003
    Scenario: Sections are numbered, a second render gets the first's words, and auditor-only notes are removed
      When "## hello" is rendered with section numbering
      Then it reads "## 1.1 hello"
      When "Spec [[1234:9.8.7.6]]." is rendered with auditor-note exclusion
      Then it reads "Spec."
      When a template lists first_pass_output.words after the words apple and banana, rendered with the vocabulary extension
      Then its second render reads "[apple][banana]"
      When numbering and note exclusion run together
      Then code in fenced blocks, tildes and inline code is left exactly as written, its "# a comment" unnumbered and its "[[1, 2]]" kept
      And only ATX headings are numbered: "#hashtag" and a lone "#" stay, "# Top" and "## Sub" become "# 1 Top" and "## 1.1 Sub"
      And a note over two lines of a paragraph, or nested in another, is removed whole: "A [[auditor" "only]] B." reads "A B."
      And a code fence inside a blockquote or a list item is code too, its notes kept
      And a note still open at the paragraph's end, "Stray [[ here", is kept as text

  Rule: Code snippets are extracted from source files for inclusion in documents

    # publishing.allium, surface CompileDhf, guarantee SnippetsFromSource
    @allium-guarantee.SnippetsFromSource
    @item-07-004
    Scenario: The lines between RDOC and ENDRDOC are a snippet under its key
      When the lines "RDOC greeting", "hello", "world", "ENDRDOC" are collected
      Then the snippet greeting is "hello" then "world"
      And lines with no markers give no snippets
      And a marker is a whole word: "PRDOC_LIMIT = 3" starts no snippet, and the snippet limit is "LIMIT = PRDOC_LIMIT"
      When a.py and b.py both hold a snippet keyed "key"
      Then collecting them is refused, naming both files
      And rdm collect exits with status 2, naming b.py

  Rule: RDM's user manual is one controlled document, published per release, that discloses every risk

    # publishing.allium, surface UserManual, guarantee ManualInReadingOrder
    @allium-guarantee.ManualInReadingOrder
    @item-07-005
    Scenario: IFU-001 lists the manual's pages in the reading order of instructions for use, behind a cover
      Given the controlled document IFU-001 and the pages it lists
      Then its chapters appear in this order: "RDM documentation", "What RDM is for", "How it works", "Limits and risks", "Install", "Quick start", "Guides", "Troubleshooting", "Reference", "Changelog"
      And every other page sits in the folder of the chapter page before it
      And the site's Docs tab shows exactly these pages, in this order
      And the first page is the cover, naming the product, "development version (after v1.1.0)", and "IFU-001, revision" with the manual's revision
      When the docs are built for the release tag v9.1.0
      Then "development version (after v1.1.0) @main" reads "v9.1.0 @v9.1.0"
      When they are built for the development version
      Then it reads "development version" and the install ref "@main"
      And no page pins a release by hand

    # publishing.allium, surface UserManual, guarantee PublishedPerRelease
    @allium-guarantee.PublishedPerRelease
    @item-07-006
    Scenario: The manual is published once per release tag and once for the development version
      Given the docs workflow and the site's configuration
      Then a release tag "v*" and a push to main both publish
      And a tag publishes under its own name and as latest, main as the version dev
      And every published version is kept on one branch, never replaced, and selectable
      And the newest release, latest, is the default

    # publishing.allium, surface UserManual, guarantee RisksDisclosedById
    @allium-guarantee.RisksDisclosedById
    @item-07-007
    Scenario: The manual's "Limits and risks" chapter discloses every risk of the register by its id
      Given RDM's risk register and the manual's "Limits and risks" chapter
      Then the chapter's risk table names every risk of the register by its id, and no other
      And each row says what the user must do about the residual risk

  Rule: The device-master-record index and the verification report are generated from the record

    # ../release/allium/release.allium, surface ReleaseEvidence, guarantee DmrIndexFromFrontmatter
    @allium-guarantee.DmrIndexFromFrontmatter
    @item-07-008
    Scenario: The DMR index has one entry per controlled document, from its frontmatter
      Given documents/sop.md with id SOP-1, revision 2, title "The SOP"
      And documents/plan.md with id PLAN-1, revision 1, title "The Plan"
      And documents/notes.md with no frontmatter
      When the DMR index data is generated
      Then it lists PLAN-1 "The Plan" documents/plan.md revision 1, then SOP-1 "The SOP" documents/sop.md revision 2
      And notes.md is named as skipped
      When the only documents have a blank id or an empty one
      Then nothing is indexed, a.md is named, and generation exits with status 1
      And the output is marked GENERATED, and generating it again gives the same file

    # ../release/allium/release.allium, surface ReleaseEvidence, guarantee VerificationReportForAReviewer
    @allium-guarantee.VerificationReportForAReviewer
    @item-07-009
    Scenario: The verification report shows a reviewer who did not run the tests what was verified
      Given a record with requirements, risks and Allure results of passing, failing and skipped runs with steps and attachments
      When the verification report is written
      Then its header names the repository, the record's commit, the commits tested, the executor and environment, the RDM version and one SHA-256 over the result files
      And the evidence is release-grade only when every requirement passed at the product's commit with a clean worktree; otherwise each reason is named
      And its anomalies list failed and skipped runs, requirements with no run, missing attachments and orphan tags
      And its traceability lists each requirement in spec order with its user needs, the risks it is a control for and its tests
      And each requirement is a baseline or a risk-based acceptance criterion, each risk shows its status and residual decision, and the register's state is summarised
      And each run shows its test's file and function, result, date and duration, failure message and trace
      And it leaves out the labels it already shows, runner internals and Allure's links
      And each step is a verification step, nested, with its own result
      And attachments show text inline up to a limit and images embedded, other files listed, the captured output and the copy of the requirement listed by SHA-256 only
      And the PDF shows all of it in that order, and an appendix lists every result file with its SHA-256
      And text from a test reaches the page as text: markup in it is shown, not run
      And without the typst package a typst executable is used, and with neither the report says so
      And the evidence bundle includes the report, rdm story evidence-report writes it, and its SHA-256 can be checked from the bundle's copy of the results
      And a result it cannot lay out leaves the reason in the bundle, not a crash
      And a symbolic link among the results is never read: its attachment is missing and its file unhashed
      And every run counts, tagged with a declared requirement or not; an unreadable or linked result, and uncommitted changes to the record, are each a reason it is not release-grade
      Given a record whose spec lives in a repository of its own, and a passing run of that repository's commit
      When the verification report is written
      Then the product's commit is the spec repository's, the record's stays its own, and the header names both
      And the run is release-grade evidence
allium/publishing.allium 
-- allium: 3
-- .pi/spec/publishing/allium/publishing.allium
--
-- Scope: the publishing context: a design history file compiled from the record
-- (Markdown templates rendered against data files, the filters of a traceability table,
-- post-processing, snippets from source) and RDM's own user manual. The surfaces are
-- the needs this context is home to: compile-dhf and user-manual (event-model/area.edn).
-- The device-master-record index and the verification report are generated here too;
-- the need they serve, release-evidence, is the release context's
-- (../../release/allium/release.allium, surface ReleaseEvidence).

------------------------------------------------------------
-- External Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- The spec RDM reads (specification): its requirements and the needs they address.
external entity Spec {}

-- The person who keeps the record.
external entity AuthorAccount {}

-- Anyone who reads RDM's user manual to keep a record the way a release enforces.
external entity Reader {}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Entities
------------------------------------------------------------

-- A Markdown document rendered from a template and the data files supplied.
entity RenderedDocument {
    template: String
    data_files: List<String>
    markdown: String
}

-- A named code snippet, from the lines between RDOC <key> and ENDRDOC in a source file.
entity Snippet {
    key: String
    source: String
    text: String
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Rules
------------------------------------------------------------

-- Render a Markdown template with Jinja2 against the data files supplied, each under
-- its file name; then post-process the Markdown (numbering, a second pass with the
-- first pass's words, auditor-note exclusion) as the render configuration names.
rule Render {
    when: Render(author, template, data_files)
    -- 1. every value the template uses is supplied by the data (refused, naming it)
    requires: for value in template.values_used: supplied(value, data_files)
    -- 2. the template exists (refused, naming it)
    requires: exists template
    ensures:
        RenderedDocument.created(template: template, data_files: data_files)
        DocumentRendered(template: template)
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Actor Declarations
------------------------------------------------------------

actor RegulatoryAuthor {
    identified_by: AuthorAccount where true
}

actor User {
    identified_by: Reader where true
}

------------------------------------------------------------
-- Surfaces
------------------------------------------------------------

-- A regulatory author can compile a design history file from the system of record:
-- the spec, the executed tests and git.
surface CompileDhf {
    facing author: RegulatoryAuthor
    context spec: Spec

    provides:
        Render(author, template, data_files)

    @guarantee SpecReadAsTaggedGherkin
        -- The spec's requirements are its Gherkin scenarios tagged with an id, each
        -- with its Feature, Rule, title, source and tags; a scenario with none is
        -- listed, never silently dropped.

    @guarantee TraceabilityFilters
        -- A template has invert_dependencies, join_to and md_indent to build a
        -- traceability table; join_to refuses an id its table lacks.

    @guarantee MarkdownPostProcessed
        -- Rendered Markdown is numbered, given the words its first render produced, and
        -- stripped of auditor-only notes, leaving code exactly as written.

    @guarantee SnippetsFromSource
        -- Code between RDOC <key> and ENDRDOC is a snippet under its key; a key
        -- collected twice is refused, naming both files.
}

-- A user learns from RDM's user manual, a controlled document of each release, how to
-- keep the record the way that release's gates enforce.
surface UserManual {
    facing user: User

    @guarantee ManualInReadingOrder
        -- IFU-001 lists the manual's pages in the reading order of instructions for use,
        -- behind a cover naming the product, its release and the manual's id and revision.

    @guarantee PublishedPerRelease
        -- The manual is published once per release tag and once for the development
        -- version; every release is kept and selectable, the newest the default.

    @guarantee RisksDisclosedById
        -- The manual discloses each risk of RDM's register by its id, with what the user
        -- must do about its residual risk.
}
